articleTitle: Construction of Comparison Systems at Solution of Radio Systems EMC Problems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Methode of comparison systems construction for EMC problems solution in radio systems with arrays are considered in the paper, including multitude access. Cases of spatial-coherent and partly-coherent receiving signals are analysed at different laws of their amplitude fading.

articleTitle: On Determining the Necessary Number of Frequency Channels for a Global HF Broadcasting Network
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In accordance with the decision taken by the WARC-HFBC-87 First Session the IFRB has performed a planning exercise. Ite results were used to estimate on increase in the number of frequency channels allocated for the HF broadcasting which is required to meet all requirements.

articleTitle: Man-Made Noise Calculation Algorithm
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with man-made noise calculation algorithm at the input of RI meter based on man-made noise signal passing through the tract consist of a band filter, a quasi-peak detector and an indicating device, whose characteristics meet CISPR requirements to RI meters.

articleTitle: Mobile Cellular Telecommunication System (MCTS) Distortions Situation Analysis
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In tne report tne computerized imitation modelling results of the distortion situation in MCTS with four types of territorial frequency planning are presented. Based on obtained calculations antenna pattern horizontal width optimizations of the base station (BS) antennas was held by criterium of signal/interference and signal/noise ratio. Radiowave propagation situation the system subband quantity and interfering BS quantity effect to electromagnetic situation in small celled MCTS were tested. The obtained results allow to form the requirements to information techniques and to choose the system parameters.

articleTitle: Study of Electromagnetic Disturbances in the Power Lines of Computing Centres
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the present paper the results of the study of the electromagnetic disturbances, that spread in the electrical networks, supplying the computing centres are given. A method is offered for determining the limits of the practical dispersal of the parameters of the disturbances on the basis of Chebishev's inequality, that is valid for an unknown law of distribution. An analysis and estimation are made of the conductive electromagnetic environment in the investigated objects.

articleTitle: The System for Evaluating Interferences in HF-Broadcasting Channels
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The system used to evaluate interference levels in HP broadcasting channels on the basis of the entries in the Tentative and Final Schedules prepared by the IFRB is described and the results are given.

articleTitle: Statistical Model of Territory Arrangement of the Sources of Mutual Interference in Land Mobile Service
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To solve a number of problems of the electromagnetic compatibility it is necessary to obtain the characteristics of electromagnetic environment EME) in the area of receiving equipment operation. The expediency of the analytical method of the construction of EME-model in the area of the mobile station operation in large cities are underlined in the report. With that objective in mind the statistical distribution of mutual distances from interference sources (base stations) ρ (R) was defined by the computer. It is shown that the distribution of ρ (R) has the form of the composition of uniform and β-distribution for the cities with the population of about 1 million and the composition of two uniform distributions for the city with the population of more than 9 millions. The values of distribution parameters are presented.

articleTitle: The Statistical Properties of Natural VLF Radio Noises in the North-East of the USSR
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: These are some results of measuring statistical properties of natural VLF radio noises taken in vicinities of Magadan, USSR North-East, 1987 to 1989. The distribution function <tex>$P(E > E_o)$</tex>, mean number <tex>$N (E > E_o)$</tex> and mean duration <tex>$\theta(E) = P(E > E_o)/ N(E > E_o)$</tex> of impulses of natural radio noise field envelope intensity (strange) have been analysed within 2 to 30 kHz carrier frequencies and different bandwidths of the receiver.

articleTitle: Cryoelectronics Elements for the Device Protecting Against EMP
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present the principle of construction of the protecting devices which operation is based on the phenomenon of a violent increase of superconductor's resistance after the loss of its superconductivity properties and a violent decrease of resistance of the bulk of the uniform doping single-crystalline silicon during avalanche breakdown as well as to review the results of investigations. The said device provides the limitation of EMP amplitude of over 4 orders of magnitude, the decrease of energy supplied to protected element of 5-7 orders of magnitude and the response time less than 0,3 ns at EMP energy of (5-50) J supplied by rectagular pulse with duration of (10<sup>−6</sup> - 10<sup>−4</sup>)s.

articleTitle: EMC in Low-Voltage Power Supply Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The consumers are connected to the low-voltage power supply networks and these ones cause the interference, the disturbance susceptible systems are operated at the same time, e.g. ripple control systems. EMC of the interfering and interfered systems in the power supply networks can be discussed by frequency characteristics of the power supply network in lots of instants. Knowlege of frequency characteristics of the power supply network is necessary especially for the evaluation of the influence of the harmonics in the power system. Frequency characteristics are considerably variable in the course of 24 hours. That's why a number of measurements in the low-voltage power distribution networks, supplying the houses area and housing estate, has been carried out. The results of frequency characteristics measurement in the low-voltage power supply networks are applicable especially for the appreciation of EMC in various power systems. The obtained knowledge is particularly significant for the evaluation of EMC in the ripple control system in the power supply networks /e.g. for the evaluation of the nonlinear-consumers influence on the ripple control system/.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Microstrip Subarray Module
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method of constructing microstrip arrays from moderate gain subarrays is presented. A four element microstrip antenna module is investigated theoretically and experimentally. Particular consideration is given to antenna parameters with respect to EMC.

articleTitle: Interference Protection Local AC Circuit in Electric Engeneering Systems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This invention relates to protection systems against interferences of electric equipment of vessels. Por saving EMC in autonomous electric engineering systems of vessels it. is suggested to use interference protection local circuits. The local circuit is separated from the rest circuit by an interference protection transformator slug. Slugs with h high effectiveness of elimination of impulsive interferences and weak capacitive influence on the supplying circuit. There is a discription of the slug and the results of exploration of its characteristics and the experience of its operation.

articleTitle: Magnetostatic Wave Band-Pass Filters with High Out-of-Band Rejection
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Magnetostatic wave filters are analysed both in the pass-band and the out-of-band in order to optimize their characteristics. The emphasis is on the out-of-band problem A filter designed provides the rejection level about 80 dB in the frequency range 1-5 GHz, while suitable parameters in the pass-band are preserved.

articleTitle: Achieving Electromagnetic Compatibility (By Development and Application of Standards)
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Progress in achieving electromagnetic compatibility is moving at an accelerated pace at the present time. Its importance in the commercial world has been emphasized by the rules being adopted in the European Community. The actions taken there are a direct result of the increasing concern which is shown in developments in standards at all levels, but especially at the international level. In the International Electrotechnical Commission a large number of the technical committees and subcommittees have prepared or are preparing requirements. There are still some difficulties that must be overcome to make this effort a truly effective one. Modeling techniques, although tremendously improved recently, still have limitations in predicting system performances. And for the purpose of setting reasonable limits and associated measurement techniques reliable statistical data on appropriate model parameters are still not generally available. In addition the proper method of dealing with the relationship of EMC design characteristics of equipments and systems safety issues needs considerable attention.

articleTitle: Generalisation of the Transfer Impedance
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The generalization of the notion of transfer impedance is proposed by means of a surface impedance. This is achieved by establishing the equivalence of losses or power transfer between two structures. A proportionality relationship between their amplitudes shows that Zs is rather independent of the structure geometry. Its application to the calculation of more complex structures is possible by appropriate modelling. The expression of Zs is given for a cylindroconical shielding from which the shielding of a circular connector with a nonuniform cross-section will be deduced.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling Through DB-25 Subminiature Connectors
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The surface transfer impedance of a variety of DB-25 subminiature connectors, such as are used on personal computer peripherals, was measured over the frequency range of 1 kHz to 100 MHz. The test samples Included die-cast and metallized plastic backshells, receptacles with and without gaskets, braid terminations that used circumferential braid terminations, such as dual cones or a compression insert, as well as strain relief devices or a simple compression set screw and a plastic backshell in which the shield was terminated to a pin and the shell of the plug by a short pigtail. All samples included several cm of braid beyond the point where the backshell made contact to the braid. The measured results will be presented along with a discussion of electromagnetic significance of each of the design features. Finally, the electromagnetic performance of these samples will be compared to that of circular connectors.

articleTitle: Calculation and Measurement of Diturbances from Lightning Discharges
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two kinds of disturbances from the lightning discharge are considered, namely, the radiation of the discharge itself and that of the metallic bodies near the discharge. The calculation is performed on the basis of the vector potential. Two types of models for setting up the discharge current are considered. The first model is the capacitor discharge to the circuit R, L. The meaning of elements R and L as well as their value are different for the process of the leader travelling and that of the main discharge. The second model, i.e. the capacitor discharge onto a long line, is more accurate. The method of B-spline approximation is used for numerical calculations. The requirements to the equipment for measuring the discharge parameters are analysed.

articleTitle: Calculating the Screening Effect of a Metal Cable Sheath with the Consideration of Nonlinearity Due to Steel Armouring
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The screening action of a steel armoured cable sheath depends on the magnitude of excitation of the armour. For practical purposes the nominal screening factor is given as a function of the longitudinal e.m.f. per unit length. Actually the screening effects of the sheath varies with resped to the sheath current rather than the e.m.f. In this paper the screening effect of a sheath is analysed by the solution of the sheath to earth circuit. The method utilizing the principles given in the new (1988.edition) CCITT Directives, is sufficiently accurate and comprehensive to consider simultanously the length varying e.m.f. and the current dependence of the outer surface impedance of the sheath. The mathematical model, i.e. system of ordinary differential equation with relevant boundary conditions, is solved by using a numerical (shooting) method and spline functions. The results of various parametric studies obtained by PC simulations are plotted in the form of graphs and tables.

articleTitle: Method and Results of Analysis of Composite Shield Characteristics
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method of estimating shield and reflection factors is developed for the case when harmonic plane electromagnetic waves are reflected by a multiple plane shield the layers of which have anisotropic conductance. The method is useful for the carbonplastic and boroplastlc shield factor analysis. The numerical analysis has revealed the fact that the factors depend on the incidence plane orientation for undirectlonal composite materials, but no dependence exists for multilayer materials with fibres interleaving in different directions.

articleTitle: Measuring Complex for Research and Prognostication of Radioelectronic Device Interferences on Stage of Designing
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The measuring complex, containing impulse-current and spark influence simulators connected to radioelectronic device cabinet(RED), and receive-registrating device, which contains super wide-range active antenna with input nuvistor, amplifier, control units with data memory, was created to research electromagnetic interference parameters. Measuring complex allows not only to estimate interference properties of REDs in real conditions of use, but allows also to realize the prognostication and correction of these properties on stage of designing of RED by means of studying: of the in interferences, which are emitted by RED model in combine with power buses, in electric mode, which is approximated to real one, at most.

articleTitle: The Effect of Weak Low-Frequency Alternating Magnetic Fields on Biological Systems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Extreme variations in the dielectric loss, conductivity, heat transfer, pH and light transmission in water systems have been observed as aftereffects of prolonged exposure of H<inf>2</inf>O, D<inf>2</inf>O and aqueous solutions of protein and rhodamine 6G (R6G) to modulated geomagnetic field at precisely fixed combinations of frequency and amplitude. The test systems have been found to retain long-term (hours) memory of the induced changes. Discussed also is the role of the protonic and deuteronic spin moments in the observed structural changes in the water.

articleTitle: Impulse Corona and ARC Discharges
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A short review will be given of the corona glow discharge from the viewpoint of its influence in determining the breakdown voltage in various gases. The growth of a subsequent high current impulse discharge from the corona leader phase, through to the blast phase is followed together with a description of electrode phenomena. Applications will be indicated in which a knowledge of these phenomena is important, in particular for EMC and EMP considerations.

articleTitle: A Time-Domain Method for Field Computation in Presence of Highly Conducting Shield of Arbitrary Cross-Section
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A time-domain procedure based on the Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) method is proposed for predicting the electromagnetic field level into two-dimensional open enclosures of arbitrary cross-section and constitutive parameters. For highly conducting materials, the TLM method is combined with analytical solutions in the time domain in order to reduce the number of memories and CPU time required by the original TLM method. Preliminary results and comparisons with known methods are presented for simple models. Extension to more complex geometries is easily implemented and cases of various shielding cavities will be presented.

articleTitle: Antennas Decoupling with the Aid of Periodical Structures
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Antennas decoupling with the aid of periodical structures having capacitive impedance is considered. Investigations based on the accuracy solution of electromagnetics boundary value problems. Elaborating mathematical models are allowed to investigate the mutial Interference between antennas located on the plane and circular cylinder. Results of numerical experiments and its analysis allowing to optimize parameters of the decoupling structures are analized. Expedient of technologicality improvement of periodical structures by it realization in the form of metal-strip lines over the dielectrical cavity is discussed.

articleTitle: Noise Immunity Analysis of Nonlinear Regenerative Filter Based on Rise Model
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This report introduces and explains the approach based on use Rise impulsive model of abnormal noise beyond the threshold point. This approach is being developed to study characteristics of nonlinear regenerative filters in response to abnormal phase fluctuations in order to determine the noise suppression probability and then to calculate noise immunity. After analization, the dependences of boundary duration phase Jump upon input signal level for various distributions of input signal amplitudes during Jump process, were obtained; then, phase fluctuations suppression probability was calculated. To determine the phase jump boundary duration criteria there have been studied the transients in nonlinear regenerative filter as a response of input signal frequency jumps with help of a computer for solving the nonlinear abbreviated differential equations.

articleTitle: Standards on Transient Disturbances in Low Voltage Power Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transient overvoltages which nay cause maloperations of equipment in low-voltage power networks are object of thorough studies in standardization organizations. These studies aim, firstly, to characterize these phenomena, as far as possible on a statistical basis. This should allow to specify emission limits and immunity tests. As for the emission limits, the report mentions that, presently, there exist only standards concerning radio broadcast protection (CISPR); the other types of transients are not yet object of standards. As for the immunity tests (IEC TO 77 & 65) several tests are considered: unidirectional surges, fast transient bursts, oscillatory waves (0.1 and 1 Khz). The report compares the main test specifications to network measurements and draw conclusions for their applicability in low voltage networks.

articleTitle: Important Characteristics of the Icc Causing EMI on PCBs and Their Values Measured on Several Types of Devices
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with EMI problems of digital devices on the PCB caused by Icc fluctuations of output drivers. Three causes of Icc increasing are explained and an advisable model of Icc current path is stated. Important characteristics of several types of devices are measured and calculated from experiments. The results of experiments are presented in the paper. From them two approaches showing how to derive the design rules for PCB are compared and one is recommended.

articleTitle: Radio Scintillation in UHF Transmissions from Earth Satellites and the Associated Ionospheric Inhomogeneities
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The tasks and method of investigation of ionospheric inhomogeneities parameters with help of satellite UHF signals are analysed. These studies are aimed at providing the most effective eleotromagnetic compatibility of various communication means and other radiating objects. The problem of radio ether "ecology" is considered. Some data on radio scintillation are given obtained during the solar eclipse in the Soviet North-East oh March 18, 1988. Their interrelation to geomagnetic activity is considered. The diurnal changes of magnetic disturbance index registered at the field station are proved to be well correlated with the observed values of scintillation index. The increased magnetic activity also results in a growth of inhomogeneities effective height and its evident variations. The data obtained during the solar eclipse testify to a considerable alteration of parameters of ionospheric inhomogeneities at that time. The wave-like disturbances seem to be due to inner gravitational waves originated while passing the eclipse front.

articleTitle: Double Differential Detection with Noise and Interference
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the error rate performance of a differential demodulation scheme for M-ary PSK signal is analysed. The demodulator under consideration is known as double differential PSK (DDPSK). It is shown that this type of demodulator can be seen as a possible candidate for employment in burst mode mobile radio communication system which is affected by Doppler shift, additive Gaussian noise and by cochannel interference. The performance comparison of DDPSK with conventional DDPSK is given.

articleTitle: Suppression of EMI Emission in a RF Plastic Welder-An Example
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper an example of effective suppression of EMI emitted by a RF plastic welder is described. The machine under consideration was constructed without taking into account the EMC problems. Recently the machine has been modernized in order to attain suppression of the primary EMI sources and their effective decoupling with the electromagnetic environment. Results of the modernization are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Vehicular Traffic and Rail Traction Radio Noise in 1-2 GHz Band
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The rail traction and petrol driven vehicles on road,generate radio noise also in the frequency band 1-2 GHz. The ignition circuitry in the vehicles, and the pantograph which makes the intermittent contacts with external power bus of electric powered local, trains, are the main sources of radio noise. The radio noise signal strength generated from petrol vehicles is of the order of −40 dBm even at a distance of 40 m from one side of a 20 m wide road, on which approximately 350 vehicles are passing in 10 minutes. Whereas the radio noise generated from rail traction line has signal strength in the range of −44 to −66 dBm. The theoretical model has also been developed to explain the observed signal strength values, and it has been found that they closely resemble.

articleTitle: Determination of the Frequency-Territory Space of Shore MF Transmitters of Maritime Mobile Service Excluding the Origin of Intermodulation Interference Based on International Recommendations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Shore transmitters of maritime mobile service provide reception of information by marine receivers in fr - mes of certain operation areas. In the range of Hectometric Waves an operational area is a sea area which is limited by a shore line and by semi-circle with radius R and a centre in the point of a transmitter location. Frequency planning of maritime mobile service is provided on the base of international recommendations. But fulfilment of the above requirements does not exclude the possibility of intermodulation interference appearance in vessel receivers under the influence of shore transmitters radiations from adjacent service zones. It is necessary to follow requirements of frequency space separations for elimination of the above. In the paper the problem is considered for intermodulation interference of the third order which is caused in a receiver by two unwanted transmitters. With the purpuse formulae are presented for calculation of minimum required the hectometric frequency-space separation transmitters of maritime mobile service, excluding intermodulation interference in frames of service area of a wanted signal transmitter. The description of frequency-space separation determination procedure is presented which provides simultaneous elimination of intermodulation interference and interference caused by the receiver blocking effect. For a number of problems to be solved in practice the field strength-vs-distance curves as well as the examples of calculations of minimum required frequency-space separations are presented.

articleTitle: Calculation of the Current and Voltage Wave Induced by Lightning in Cable Lines
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the cable lines stretched along an insulating inviroment a great overvoltage caused by lightning dischardes above them are observed. The phenomenon of numerous cable damage at great distances from the thundercloud above the cable caused by a single miss lightning hit is also known. According to the widespread explanation of these effects the overvoltage is a result of the influence of the electromagnetic waves radiated by a lightning current.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Distortions of MSK Signal on Noise Immunity of Coherent Reception
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Under real conditions a signal differing from the one for which the receiver i3 intended. Causes of distortions may he different: imperfect operation of transmitter, filtration, multipath propogation, etc. This paper describes attempt to evaluate the quantity of distortions by distortion factor K<inf>d</inf>. The value of K<inf>d</inf>. is connected with energy losses caused by signal distortions.

articleTitle: Interference Environmental Classes, Test Requirements for Apparatus and Measures for Interference Reduction in HV Substations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During switching operations or faults in HV substations and during atmospheric discharges, voltages of high value and high frequency are generated in secondary circuits. HV substations and their parts have been classified into four environmental classes. Apparatus within the classified environment are to be tested in accordance with IEC Standards and tests applied at the "Milan Vidmar" Institute during switching operations in primary circuits.

articleTitle: Rigorous Analysis of Diffraction in a TEM Cell
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work two different techniques for the prevision of the induced current density and of the scattered field by a conductive body inside a TEM cell are presented. The former is based on the Moment Method Exact Green's Function (MM/EG) and is applied in the frequency domain. The second is a particular algorithmic form of finite difference equations in the time domain (FDTD).

articleTitle: Analysis of Antimultipath Techniques in Cellular Mobile Communication Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper some methods to combat multipath radio propagation in Digital Cellular Mobile Communication Systems (DCMCS) are considered. Simulation aspects for multipath pattern as a function of urban building density and heights of transmitting and receiving antennas are also discussed. The greatest attention has been paid to wideband techniques for the case of PCM usage and estimation of quality parameters concerning received radio signals has been obtained.

articleTitle: The Enhancement of the Interference-Killing Feature of the FM Signal Receivers Through the Use of Parametric Frequency Dividers in the Intermediate Frequency Channel
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the study of the signal and interference mixture frequency split procedure it was determined the signal-interference ratio increases in direct proportion to the division ratio squared. This phenomenon takes place under the conversion of the signal to the non-additive form. This can be done by restricting the oscilation amlitude when the total ascillation level is one order higher than the restriction level of the delimiter.

articleTitle: The Prediction of the Voltage and Current Levels Induced in the Aircraft Side Circuits Struck by the Lightning
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article describes the methods of estimation the voltage levels induced in the side circuits of the aircraft struck by the lightning. It also, describes the interaction of the lightning currents flowing through the fuselage and the aircraft wings with the communication lines layed in them. The voltages induced in this circuits have been determined taking into account the wing geometry, fuselage shape and the availability of slots in wings and apertures in fuselage. The determination technique of voltages induced by the lightning currents in the aircraft side circuits is brought up to the engineering design level. The realiability of the technique developed is confirmed experimentally with the results discordance not more than 15%.

articleTitle: Effect of Low Intensiti Elektromagnetic Field on Stress Resistance of Micro-Organisms
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work the energetic effects of constant and alternating fields (mainly over the radio frequency and extremely high frequency ranges) are considered. It is reported the results of experiments carried out for filling the gap existing at the present time in our ideas in relation to the possibility to electroadaptation of microbial cells to the stress action by means of radio frequency and extremely high frequency (EHF) fields of low (till 0,1 W) and superlow (till 0,01 W) intensity. The results in relation to the stress resistance after treating with electromagnetic (EM) filds over the above-mentioned frequency ranges are presented on an example of microbial cells Esheriohia coli M-17. For this culture we studied the action of EM-fields over the EHF range with a wave-lenght at which no resonance biological effects had been revealed so far (in our oase <tex>$\lambda = 6$</tex>, 2mm). As objects for research we applied also another types of micro-organisms: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Streptomyces spheroides. On an example of these micro-organisms it was demonstrated the effect of EM-field over the EHF range on the capability for resisting the depressing action of metabolic inhibitor (detergent, culture reduced temperature).

articleTitle: Computation of Limits on Frequency-Space Separation of One-Channel VHF Radio Relay Stations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Frequency-space separation (FSS) of radio stations is one of the main methods for EMC provision of radio means. In this connection a number of works is dedicated to establishment of radio means FSS limits. In this paper the problem is considered as applied to duplex one-channel VHP radio relay stations which are used for organization of radiotelephone communication by transmission of frequency-modulated signals through radio-relay lines. The formulae for calculation of the minimum required FSS of duplex one-channel radio relay stations are presented in the paper. They determine probability of provision of radio relay stations depending on the degree of electromagnetic interaction between radio stations. The computation procedure of the limited values of FSS which guarantees the EMC of the one-channel radio relay stations with the predetermined probability is presented. For a number of problems to be solved in practice the plots are presented which permit to determine the required parameters of the formulae including dependence of radio waves propagation losses. Examples of derivation of FSS limits of radio relay stations are presented.

articleTitle: Radio Astronomy and WARC 92
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Man-made interference of various kinds has an increasingly negative impact on observational astronomy. Many, if not all radio astronomical observing sites have experienced some types of effects degrading the observations. A strategy to coordinate world-wide action should be refined, while communication with active radio services and responsible administrations should be intensified. This is in particular urgent in view of a general World Aministrative Radio Conference, WARC, which will be held in 1992 under auspices of the International Telecommunications Union. During this WARC all allocations of frequencies between 0.5 and 3 GHz may be reconsidered together with those to ‘new services’ at frequencies above 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Progress in Modern EMI Test Instrumentation
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes the efficient use of microprocessor intelligence in test receivers for the detection and analysis of EMI. Progress in hardware, especially in synthesized local oscillators is accompanied by a corresponding progress in firmware. The process of concentrating computing intelligence closer to the analog hardware has continued. Work that has previously been the task of an external controller will in future be done by the test receiver itself. The result is a compact, intelligent and flexible system. Test receivers will no longer only scan the input spectrum but will also be able to analyze it and compare it to the specification limits. The paper treats strategies for optimum signal detection and it will show that flexibility is needed for different situations. In cases where quasi peak and average limits have to be taken into consideration a prescan may be done with a peak and an average detector at the same time. The critical points of the EMI spectrum may automatically be extracted for time consuming tests like quasi peak weighting. The simultaneous use of the peak detector with a weighting detector in conjunction with the microprocessor firmware helps to optimize autoranging procedures with weighting detectors like average and quasi peak. Even for manual use of test, receivers without a spectrum display the microprocessor can give the user the necessary orientation aid. Besides that the test receiver's I/O interfaces can control the most important coupling devices, the antenna mast and EuT turntable and it will be enabled to produce the complete test reports and to save test results. In other words: the test receiver will be self-contained.

articleTitle: A Parametric Study of EMI Coupling with Electronic Subsystems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic coupling effects on circuits containing distributed elements (e.g., connection wires, buses, etc.) are considered. A low-frequency approximation based on a lumped-element model is shown to be valid up to the first line resonance. The suitability of the model for a wide range of frequencies is obtained by means of a careful location of the sources that account for coupling. The model predicts also that the immunity of the system worsens as the incidence direction of the interfering plane wave shifts from the vertical. A transmission fine model approach is used to validate the lumped circuit and to extend the susceptibility analysis to higher frequencies. Numerical simulations evidence worst-case situations for the circuit immunity, as a function of the wire distance from the ground and the line termination.

articleTitle: EMP Coupling to Cable with Matched Load
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the solution of EMP coupling to infinite shieldid cables with matched load. The diffraction problem in the frequecy domain is solved. The calculated fields are used to estimate the voltage on matched load. This calculation is based on long line model with distributed sources and inverse Fourier transformation. Normal and oblique incidence of EMP is investigated. The influence of the earth is not taken into account. The numerical results are also discussed.

articleTitle: Fluctuations of the Coefficient of Depolarization at Propagation of Microwaves
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results of experimental investigation of spatial and time fluctuations of the coefficient of depolarization which is the ratio of the cross polarization field intensity to the signal level at the main polarization are described. Experiments are performed along two paths with dominant obstacles at 10 cm wavelength.

articleTitle: Automated Electromagnetic Spectrum Monitoring System Aboard the Aircraft
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The spectrum monitoring requirements for the electromagnetic situation analysis aboard the aircraft are stated. A structure of digital spectrum analizer attached to the various computing systems aboard and the object tested are given. A new method of factorization for determing harmonic component parameters is presented and its comparison with the Fast Fourier Transform algorithms is given. A new configuration of the high quality narrow-band digital filter is described.

articleTitle: Double B Method for Interference Prediction and Coordination
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, an interference prediction & coordination method, i.e. the Double B Method, is proposed, a clarification about the definition of isolation between two satellite networks is given, and a unified derivation process for the interference prediction & coordination methods appeared in the past ages is presented for the convenience of making comments.

articleTitle: Variations of Scattering Index Modulus at V.H.F Band in Urban Streets
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Urban multipath propagation at v.h.f. and u.h.f. bands is conditioned by reflections and wave diffractions from buildings and other constructions. The intensity of the scattering field depends on diffracting and screening features of the city objects. A statistical approach is given to determine the averaged meaning of the modulus of the scattering index at a local site in the street and its variations in different reception conditions.

articleTitle: Safety of Telecommunications Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: CENELEC is preparing an European Norme (EN) to specify the additional safety precautions that must be taken when electrical equipment, e.g. a computer, is connected to a telecommunications network. The EN is still being prepared but the subject is being aired for general discussion since international electrical safety standards have not yet included telecommunications networks. The paper explains some of the new concepts included in the provisional European Norme (prEN)<sup>1</sup> and illustrates the way in which existing telecommunications practices are being incorporated.

articleTitle: EMI Shielding for Plastic Enclosures
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic, or Radio Frequency Interference (EMI/RFI) can have devastating effects on electronic devices. Corruption of computer data, malfunction of vital equipment, or loss of communications can all be caused by the transient energy generated by electronic circuitry. Advances in IMI shielding technology have tended to be led by defence industry requirements, but the need for shielding is now becoming just as vital in the commercial sector. The forthcoming regulations from the EEC will have major repercussions throughout consumer, industrial, and commercial electronics manufacturing industries, increasing the awareness of EMI shielding requirements. Recent developments in this area include the introduction of a high technology process for shielding plastic enclosures. Based upon the electroless plating technique, the process is capable of producing a thin uni form copper and nickel coating on substrate surfaces, giving a minimum of 70dB of shielding effectiveness (SE) over a wide frequency range. This is up to 40dB improvement in SE over existing methods of shielding plastic enclosures.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Calculation in Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the most obvious tendencies in mechanical engineering is an increase of installed equipment density. It results in the fact that power supply network and signal network in particular are influenced by crosstalk because of close installation of networks and separata channels installation inside one network. Economical, light and flexible flat cables are mostly influenced by crosstalk.

articleTitle: Asymmetry of Reactions of Human Central Nervous System to Electromagnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic fields (EMF) are physical factors of the medium, which significantly influences the living organisms. Biological effect of this influence is defined by biotropic parameters of the field - its frequency, intensity, signal form, vector direction, etc. A man in modern life is subjected to the action of not only natural, helio-geophysical EMF, but also the artificial ones, appeared as a result of civilization development. In this connection there is an acute problem on "compatability" of man with the EMF penetrating into its environment.

articleTitle: Freguency Assignment and Figer of Merit of Radio Eguipment
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A connection between freguncy assignment and EMC parameters of radio eguipment is considerent. The number of channels which can be used simultaneously by transreceivers is usually considerably less than the total number of channels in the freguency range. The reason of this is mutnal electromagnetic interferences among radiostations. Freguency channel denial to the user depends on not only interference level in the channel but also on EMC parameters of the radio eguipment. This, efficiency of utilization of the freguency range in a given electromagnetic environment might serve as an EMC Figure of Merrit (FOM) of the eguipment.

articleTitle: Millimeter Waveguide Limiter
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The result of experimental investigations of the millimeter waveguide limiters constructed on the basis of the NbN thin film superconductor are presented in this paper. In the "open" state at the band-pass (5-10)%, an insertion loss of (0.5-1)dB is ensured while in the "limitation" state the said lose amounts ≳ 20dB in the large frequency range. The response time of device is < 10<sup>−9</sup> s.

articleTitle: Cable Products and Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper has a purpose to suggest an improved model for inner intensity calculation in a coaxial noise-supressing cable with a braided outer conductor, in which monochromatic noise current flows. The model is specific in using more accurate parameters of the cable substitution schemes transfer impedance, propagation coefficient and wave impedance. A procedure has been shown and justified, which enables to narrow discrepancy between transfer impedance predictions and measurements for frequencies over 1 MHZ. The prosedure is recommendable for braided shields with the fill of the braid lead than 85%. For this purpose the geometry coefficient is determined, which is largely dependent on the braiding technique of a specific producer. The paper also advocates the use of noise-supressing sheaths in cables. Combined use of the sheaths and braided shields secures cable noise immunity in a wide frequency range from 0.01 MHZ to 1 HHZ without a considerable weight increase and loss in flexibility. Restriction of incidental electromagnetic noise (IEN) is a topical problem of the electromagnetic compatibility of radio-electronic equipment (EMC REE). The source of noise is largely a quasiaerial behaviour of shield cables, related to the reception and radiation of electromagnetic field energy in neighbouring and remote zones, and propagation of an induced current through cables toward terminals.

articleTitle: In Vivo Electrostimulation of Osteoporotic Bone using a Modulated Radiofrequency Field
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There is evidence that integrity of our skeletal is affected by out dietary mineral intake<sup>1</sup>. Osteoporisis is characterised by the loss of mineralized tissue, which results in structural failures despite continued functional demands. The influence of dietary calcium and phosphorus in the occurrence of skeleton diseases of the growing and the aged, notably senile osteoporisis is therefore a matter of currant interest. Several studies suggest that prolonged calcium deprivation may lead to osteoporisis.<sup>2,3</sup> In addition to alterations in dietary calcium, the concentration of phosphate in the diet has profound effects on the calcium transport system. The close relationship between the skeleton and metabolism of calcium and phosphorous is demonstrated by findings that the amounts of calcium and phosphorous in skeleton decrease when a low phosphorous diet is fed and phosphorous retention is controlled by the rate of calcium retention which in itself is directly related to calcium absorption<sup>4</sup>. Thus a low calcium or low phosphate content or combination in diet induce a disturbance in the bone mineralization process<sup>5</sup>. There are also evidences that supplementation of the diets with calcium, calcitonin, vitamin D and exercise may increase bone density and contribute towards prevention of the early onset of osteoporosis<sup>6</sup>. As the probability of fracture is closely related to effective bone mass, a modality that could prevent or retard loss of bone might provide a substantial reduction in the incidence of skeletal morbidity.

articleTitle: The Influence of Lightning's Approximation on the Transient Response of Horizontal Ground Electrodes
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the influence of the shape of the injected lightning current on the voltage distribution and distribution of first current derivation by time along a horizontal ground electrodes. To determine these distributions a suitable mathematical description of the lightning current is needed. The values taken by means of generally known approximations were compared with values determined by lightning currents recorded at measuring stations in order to find the best approximation.

articleTitle: Sharing Techniques for Using the Radio Spectrum in the Year 2000
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the technical, operational and administrative factors that should be considered to effectively share the spectrum in the year 2000. Increasing spectrum requirements of individual radio services can only be met in the future by effectively sharing time, space or frequency. Both intraservice and inter-service sharing is required. Sharing procedures need to be computer automated and vary from simple deterministic procedures, to complex statistical procedures. Successful sharing of the spectrum in the future is not limited by technical constraints or computational methods but rather by radio service requirements that limit agreements on acceptable sharing criteria between services.

articleTitle: Wrocław EMI-ITE Laboratory
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When testing computing devices end other digital equipments for electromagnmetic compatibility there are two important aspects to consider: susceptibility testing and emission testing. This paper describes measuring facilities for both emission and susceptibility testing erected at the laboratory for investigations of Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) caused by the Information Technology Equipment (ITE) and the susceptibility of this equipment to the electromagnetic disturbances (Wroclaw EMI-ITE Laboratory).

articleTitle: On Problems of Designing Impulse Noise Line Filters
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Line filters occupy an Important place in solving the problem or electro-magnetic compatibility of REE (radio electronic equipment). Theoretically, they can be divided into two glasses) radio interference and impulse filters, the latte being designed for impulse noise (discontinuous jamming) suppression appearing as the result of commutational processes in power circuits and which are tranfered to the consumer by conductance. Such impulse noise may be of high values (from 1000 to 1500 W) with varied duration (from nanosecond up to hundreds microseconds) under the steep front increase. Reaching the consumer it considerably affects the operational reliabiluty of REE and especially digital computer device end in some oases causes the equipment failure.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Fields as Favorable Factors to Soliton Creation in the Periodical Biological Structures
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method for description of solitons propagating in the periodic and quasiperiodic biological structures has been developed. For further further description of soliton in the biological structures the energy of the electromagnetic fields was taken into account. The threshold values of electric vector of EM fields for a possible creation of solitons in DNA were also considered.

articleTitle: Effect of the Current Fluctuations on the Side Lobe Radiation in Antennas
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper concerns the effect of fluctuations in the amplitude and phase distribution of sources on the antenna's side lobe radiation. It is shown that the side lobe radiation level defining considerably the EMC of radio electronic devices is very sensitive to the presence of "randomness" in the antenna. Different aspects of this problem are discussed conformably to the far zone and to the Fresnel zone for antennas of different types: continuous and discrete (regular and irregular antenna arrays). A number of curves characterizing variation of the side lobe radiation in antennas of different types versus the sources statistics in the antenna and observation point location are cited. Besides the local field characteristics there are given the antenna integral power field characteristics allowing to see how the power radiated by the antenna is distributed between various angular sectors on different antenna ranges. It is pointed out that the sources fluctuations in the antenna limit the minimal attainable level of its side lobe radiation.

articleTitle: Summary of the Report: "Investigation of the Combined Method of the Frequency Modulated Signal Formation with Enhanced EMC"
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: FM-signal can be formed either by a direct method, by which the stability of the carrier is low, or by an indirect method, with the help of phase modulation. by which the medium frequency stability is low and it is hard to transmit the low frequencies of the modulating signal (MS), that is the signals with high duration. Finally, there is no possibility to transmit the constant component of the modulating signal, where by the modulator sensitivity to the noise, especially in the range of MS high frequencies, remains, great, what declines the noise immunity and EMS of systems.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Interference Influence on Electronic Equipment via its Grounding System
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The influence of the electromagnetic field produced by vertically-polarized plane sine wave on the electronic system represented as a sphere and a straight grounding wire (of the length, h), parallel to the vector of the electric field strenght of the plane wave of interference is outlined. The possibility of the execeeding of the total magnetic field produced. by the effect indicated by an order in magnitude in the V wavelenght range, when 5h λ 100h, and almost by two orders in magnitude at the frequency of the first resonance in thesystem in comparison to the magnetic field of the affecting plane wave is shown.

articleTitle: Interferences of Microwave Power Installations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper reviews the important regulations pertaining to interferences from microwave power equipment and reports on the measured levels and spectra. The envelopes of these spectra are irregular and it is demonstrated that the interferences of emissions from these unstable signals in a telecommunication channal are very low. The emissions or leakage levels for reducing the probability of these interferences are discussed. Methods for avoiding leakages in particular at the illegal 900 MHz are presented. The actual industrial situation of the microwave power applications urgently demands for a legal ISM frequency in the 900 MHz band, with a reasonable limit of 60 dBµV/m at 30m from the building.

articleTitle: Metal Corrosion under the Intermittent EMI Effect of Power Line
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The intermittent EMI voltage can cause pilling on the surface of the underground pipeline, but the pit depth was smaller. The intermittent EMI has very different corrosivity, therefore it is suggested to give a more detaile research on the intermittent EMI corrosion. In same condition, the criterion for the intermittent EMI voltage should be large than continue EMI.

articleTitle: Antenna Coupling Reduction by Shields
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of aspects of electromagnetic compatibility is a problem connected with reduction of the coupling between transmitting and receiving antennas placed in the vicinity of each other. This problem can be solved using metallic or absorbing screens. Dimensions of the shields are limited as a rule, by antenna patterns, observation sectors and other factors. Therefore the choice of the screen shape and absorbing material is very important, when providing the high shielding efficiency.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Hazards for Biological Systems and Strategy of Electromagnetic Compatibility Control
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Biological and epidemiological data indicate that electromagnetic fields exert adverse effects oh the living organisms including humans. Electromagnetic radiations bring about impairment of the regulatory functions affecting nervous and endocrine systems, As a result of long-term exposure to electromagnetic fields some functional and morphological abnormalities were found in different systems including suppression of immune reactions, promotion of malformations and organ dysfunctions. The strategy of ALARA ( As Low As Reasonably Achievable) is suggested to control electromagnetic compatibility with biological systems in their natural environment.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Antenna Properties of Telephone-Subscriber Lines
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: IEC/TC77/WG6 has been assigned the task of describing and classifying the EM environment. The results should form the basis for EMC requirements with respect to equipment to be installed in that environment. In case of equipment to be connected to an extended network, e.g. that formed by telephone-subscriber lines, the antenna properties of the network, ie. its unintentional EM coupling properties, have to be known before a relevant description and classification are possible. The characterization of these antenna properties call for a statistical approach and consequently so does the classification.

articleTitle: Application Possibilities of Semiconductive Materials for Telecommunication Cables
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In connexion with the increasing amount and performance of different EMI sources and with contemporary decreasing levels of transmitted signals the problem concerning telecommunication cables screening is permanently growing large. Increased signification of the new atypical screening materials is given by the requirement of high quality transmission and also by getting optimal material and technology costs at screening production.

articleTitle: The Registration of LEMP on Telecommunication Lines inside Buildings
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During a period of 1 - 2 years, overvoltages surpassing a certain level were registrated on 10 telecommun. lines inside transmitter towers and on 9 lines inside large buildings. Three different types of registration devices were used. The results of measurings presented in this paper are expressed in terms of overvoltage number per thunderstorm day and classified into 2 groups according to the screening of the lines. They show the importance of solving the problem of atmospheric overvoltage protection of equipment connected to lines inside buildings.

articleTitle: Progress in the Study of EMC. Reminiscences and the Future
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The term "Electromagnetic Compatibility" was generally introduced in 196A, when the IEEE Group on Radio Interference changed its name to IEEE Group on Electromagnetic Compatibility and made analogous changes in the name of its periodicals. In the new style issue (Jan. 1964) Herman Garlan wrote: "Electromagnetic Compatibility is not new". Though this word was first used in military electronics, the concept behind the word was not new. The first conscious effort to take into account all factors: oscillator radiation, receiver selectivity, image response, intermodulation, was in the table of assignments for UHF-TV channels, adopted by FCC in 1952. J.T. Dixon gave a talk in 1963 about the assignment of UHF-TV channels, taking into account certain "taboos", technical constraints in the assignment of television channels. He used this term, before he had heard of "electromagnetic compatibility" or "spectrum singnatures", or other terms as exotic! Even the chairman of the EMC Group expresses some doubts: What does electromagnetic compatibility really mean? What are the EMC performance acceptability criteria? Do we make the change in order to impress our contracts? As I see it, the advantage of the new title was, that it stressed a positive effect, and before we had stressed the negative aspect: radio interference.

articleTitle: Interaction Effects in Cylindrical Arrays of Microstrip Antennas with Multilayered Enclosure
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analysis of cylindrical periodic arrays of rectangular printed antenna elements is approached for elements fed by corporate microstrip lines. The approach is based on the solution of the exitation problem of the periodic array nested into the layered dielectric enclosure of an infinite metallic cylinder. The explicit expressions are derived for central array element fed at the arbitrary chosen point. The computations are performed for a linear polarized array. Presentation is made of radiation patterns components affected by an array conformal cover. Dielectric coating layer placed over arrays on cylinders of moderate electrical diameter shapes and flattens azimuthal patterns and reduces radiation in aft hemisphere.

articleTitle: EMI Circuit Model of Buried Pipeline under the Effect of Power Line
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The calculation for electromagnetic interference voltages on the pipeline, has always been presented with some errors, makes the design for pipelines or power lines not only conservative bul also expensive. The source of error is incorrect values of electrical parameters. A reasonable and practical circuit model for the calculation of EMI voltage on the buried pipeline is presented from finding of IT field tests. According to interpretation of our data obtained from the field tests, some distributed parameters vary with the EMI voltages and with distance. Therefore the differential equations for the circuit model should be variational coefficient equations. A practical method for the calculation of EMI voltages on the pipeline is presented, the errors obtained by this calculation is less than 22%, which meets the demand of practical application.

articleTitle: An Overview of CISPR Work on EMC
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: International cooperation on matters of radio interference began in 1933 when an informal conference was held in Paris between representatives of several organisations. The conference agreed that the main objective was to achieve uniformity in the methods of controlling interference in order to facilitate exchange of appliances between countries. The main recommendation of the conference was that a joint commission should be set up by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the International Union of Broadcasting (UIR). The recommendation was implemented and the International Special Committee on Radio Interference was formed.

articleTitle: Estimation of Electromagnetic Pulse Parameters Through Inverse Filtering Using Wiener Transform
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a method for estimation of electromagnetic pulse parameters when only values of instantaneous voltage on probes loads and modulus of transfer function of test circuit are available has been presented. The method is based on inverse filtering in time domain. Some results of applying the method to the signals measured in Electromagnetic Pulse Laboratory has been presented.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Forecasting Methodic Based on Indirect Criterion
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It's necessary to take into account switch-mode power supply parasitic parameters (PP) of regular components, construction and mounting when explore the power supplies high frequency elektromagnetic interference(EMI) forecasting methodic.

articleTitle: Determining the Electric Parameters of the Crawford Cell
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discribes one of the measuring set-ups equipped with TEH Crawford cell. This set-up was erected at the Wroclaw EMI-ITE Laboratory. An effective technique for the numerical modeling of the TEH cell is presented. The calculated characteristics of the input impedance are compared with relevant values obtained by measurement.

articleTitle: Measurement and Analysis Formula of the Transfer Impedance of Multiconductor Shielded Cables
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recent research in measurement and analysis of the transfer impedance of a kind of multicoductor shielded cables is presented. Especially, one method of getting the analytical frequency formula of the transfer impedance of the measured multiconductor shielded cable is expressed.

articleTitle: Space-Time Model Adapted in Terms of Schuman Resonance Frequency Range
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The frequency range extending into the Schuman resonance domain is considered for the model of absolute, values of ELF radio noise E<sub>z</sub>-component. The article publication considers the space-time model of absolute levels E<sub>z</sub>, which is the natural radio noise component, within 60 to 500 c/s range. At this [1] the world thunderstorm sites model is underlain by CCIR (International Radio Consultative Committee) map data analysed. Then, the summarized field absolute value' is calculated for the point of reception with the help of the effective current moments estimated of the world thunderstorm sites and their geographic coordinates represented in CCIR maps. These calculations are performed in terms of electrodynamic problem solution for the absolutely conductive spherical Earth with homogeneous anisotropic ionosphere taken in asymptotic approximation [3]. At this, the time dependence of the source current moment is expressed as exp(jωt) with invariable phase, which results in the field evidently expressed nodes and crests within the Schuman resonance range. At this, according to experimental evidences, the time averaging being 6 to 8 minutes, the standing wave nodes and crests are suppressed due to natural radio noise phase randomness. To make the calculated field stochastic, the summerized field is proposed to determine as summing up powers of direct and backward waves. Thus, for the space-time model [1] the calculative expression is proposed to use representing the field as a sum of direct and backward waves repeatedly running over the Earth [2]. This expression has been verified for its fitness within the Schuman resonance frequency range in relation to the results obtained with the help of exact formulae of zonal harmonios sum [3]. The criterion has been also determined to take into account the quantity of the world direct and backward waves. Their adequate correspondence has been testified to by the qualitative comparison between the spectrum characteristics calculated for the Schuman resonance eight modes, as well as their peak diurnal variations, and the experimental evidences obtained in Magadan, USSR, in summer. The available high latitude experimental evidences on the field spectrum characteristics absolute values (Barrow, USA) [6] have been accompanied by their theoretical calculations, which also verify the proposed representation of the calculated field at a considerable time of its averaging.

articleTitle: Considerations on Measurements of Radio Interference from the Electrical Appliances by a Shortened Procedure According to CISPR Recommendations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Measurements procedure of products-sources of man-made interferences accepted in CISPR is carried out by a random sample of products taken from a batch of typical appliances. In this case the fulfilment of "80% - 80%" rule should be guaranteed. According to the rule the highest probability to approve "unconditioned" products as "conditional" ones (consumer's risk) is equal to 0,2. Statistical assesment of compliance with the limit is fulfiled on the basis of probabilities non-central t-distribution and binomial distribution. At evaluation by the binomial distribution of probabilities the value of the consumer's risk is ensured at the sample of n=7 items providing all items in the sample comply with the limit. But the "80%-80%" basis accepted in CISPR is not fulfiled actually, because in accordance with CISPR 14 type tests can be made on one item only. As it is shown in the paper, the consumer's risk in this case rises upto 0,8, i.e. "unconditioned" products may be approved as "conditioned" ones. In the paper conditions are studied at which the required value of consumer's risk 0,2 is ensured as well as the rule "80%-80%". The realization of the conditions it's necessary to evaluate man-made interferences according to more stringent requirements, as it is accepted when using non-central t-distribution. Degree of the tightening depends on the sample volume and mean - root-square deviation of the man-made interference from individual sources. Value of the deviation may be accepted on the base of generalization of experimental data. Degree of the tightening is determined at reduction of the sample volume down to examination by single appliances.

articleTitle: Direction Finding of Equatorial-Latitude Whistlers and Their Propagation
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Spaced direction finding measurement for very low latitude whistlers has been carried out at three stations, Zhanjlang(geomag.lat. 10.1°), Guilin (14.1°) and Wuchang(19.4°) in South China in January 1988. The following new experimental findings are obtained from this campaign, (1) The ionospheric exit region of whistlers is very much restricted to the geomagnetic latitude range of 10°–14°, (2) the extent of their ionospheric exit region is very stable on different days, and the radius of the distribution is less than 40–50km, (3) surprisingly high occurrence of echo-train whistlers is observed, and (4) the propagation of whistlers in the Earth-ionosphere waveguide after the ionospheric transmission is more plausible toward higher latitudes than toward the equator and the subionospheric propagation seems to exhibit a horizontal beam. Discussions by making use of these experimental facts have indicated that the whistlers observed in the geomagnetic latitude range from 10° to 14° are attributed to field-aligned propagation, but there are many interesting problems to solve in future.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Attenuation by Box-Type Covers
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The main purpose of the shielding theory is to give radioelectronics engeneers a possibility to estimate levels of interferences passing through covers. Metal boxes of radioelectronic means have a number of definite features which complicate the shielding problem. The conclusions and calculationc for idealized covers presented in publications cannot give us exact results. Prom the experience we know that tha most exact results can be means of data based on the special analysis of shielding cover classes separately selected.

articleTitle: Channel Technique Prediction of EMC REM at SRF
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the report the present condition, metrological facility, problems and prospects of channel technique prediction of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of radioelectronic means (REM) at secondary radiation frequences is discussed.

articleTitle: EMI Reduction Techniques in Traction Measurements
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Thyristor locomotives generate EMI of high intensity. Some typical values of EMI appearing in measuring circuits during the locomotive test are given in the paper. Examples are taken from practical experiments. Main possibilities of EMI reduction techniques verified during traction measurements as well as experiencies concerning the EMI reduction possibilities are described.

articleTitle: Influence of Cable Connectors on EM Coupling of Electrical Circuits
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Cable connectors can increase EM coupling of electrical circuits in shipboard cable runs. It is important to obtain EMC in shipboard cable runs with connectors and boxes. Calculation of coupling parameters can be performed on the base of conductor sizes only in simple cases. Suggested impulse technique of mutual inductance and capacitance measurements in cable connectors give possibility to measure coupling from 0.1 nH and 0.01 pF. The results of measurements and calculations give possibility to estimate the influence of cable connectors on EM coupling and induced voltages in screened and nonscreened different circuits. The results are useful for induced pulse voltage estimating and connector design.

articleTitle: Databank for EMC Standards
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Intense activity in the field of Electromagnetic Compatibility Standardization in the various Committees dealing with this subject, makes it very difficult to get a complete overview on all existing documents or documents in progress. In order to overcome this problem, an extended databank has been realized. It Includes: • Basic EMC Standards • Products EMC Standards The Basic Standards are grouped according the the classification of IEC: • description of the EMC phenomena • limits • testing & measuring techniques • installation guidelines The paper will give a survey of the work done to collect the most significant information on existing EMC Standards, to organize them in a data-bank and give a tool to enable a selection as a function of their nature (Basic or Product related), their applicability to the different environmental requirements, different products and installations.

articleTitle: EMF Induce Levels in ESP Cable Lines
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper contains an estimation of the levels of voltages induced in cable lines of electroenergetic systems (EES) of means of transport and electrophysical installations under the influence of external electromagnetic fields. The theory of line transfer has been used for constructing a mathematical model. The results of calculations have been compared with those of the experiment.

articleTitle: Effects of Rainfall on the Utilization of 30/20 6Hz Satellite Communicatin Links
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Present microwave line of sight radio relay systems operate in frequency bands in the neighbourhood of 2GHz, 4GHz, 66Hz. 128Hz and 148Hz according authorized frequency bands approved by the international Telecommunication Union (ITU) through special World Adminstrative Radio Conferences (WARC'S). Rain attenuation is currently recognised as an important factors in designing and hence succesful operation of microwave communication links. Although signal attenuation caused by rainfall is of negligible importance at 26Hz band, it becomes of increasing concern as the frequency increases. Specifically at frequencies above 10 6Hz, rainfall has considerable effect and it offers severs limitation on system performance and reliability. Cosequently the path length of terrestrial radio systems may necessarly severly limited to allow acceptable signal-to-noise ratio with conventional. transmitters and receivers. In satellite communications, rain attenuation is currently occur since rainy paths could be relatively much longer as compared to terristrial microwave links and certinally of variable lengths.

articleTitle: Statistical Evaluation of Pattern Ripple of Antennas Situated on Movable Objects
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Theoretical models are proposed for evaluation of the pattern ripple of low directive and highly directive antennae. The correlations for F (k ≤ K) are calculated, the numerical results are presented. Experimental check up of instantaneous patterns is carried out, its statistical characteristics are determined.

articleTitle: Limits Estabilshment of EMC Parameters of Vehicle Electrical Equipment and Radio Receiver
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The experience on the vehicle radio receiver operation shows that at present the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of a radio receiver and an electrical network of a vehicle in all the broadcast frequency bands is not ensured.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation Indicators
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The work presents electromagnetic radiation indicators designed at the Technical University of Wroclaw.
