The indicators are destined for personnel working in the vicinity of EM radiation sources as a personal protection means. Presented designs work within 27.12 MHz and 2.45 GHz ISM bands. Their sensitivity is in accordance with Polish labour safety standards and general public protection standards. The problem of mutual interaction of the indicators measuring antenna and a human body was taken into account and estimated, the results were implemented into designs and standarization procedures.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation Spectrum Emitted by a Negative Corona Discharge D.C. Source Supplied
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of measurement of the frequency characteristics of electromagnetic interference (electric and magnetic component) generated by the negative corona discharge and mixed discharge composed of the bridged corona and the repeated spark discharge are presented. The discharge was performed in the air or in the 16 % CO<inf>2</inf>/N<inf>2</inf> mixture under the atmospheric pressure between the set of 7 negative polarized needle electrodes and the positive plate electrode. The discharge was d.c. supplied. As the results show, the electromagnetic interference in the spectral range from about 0.01 MHz to tens MHz is generated by both discharges. The intensity of the magnetic component of the interference field is lower than its electric component. The electromagnetic interference of the lowest intensity is generated by the d.c.-featured bridged negative corona discharge. Higher interference is emitted by the low-current pulsed. Trichel corona and the mixed discharge. The negative corona and mixed discharge in the CO<inf>2</inf>/N<inf>2</inf> mixture, simulating exhaust gases generate electromagnetic interference of the intensity higher than that produced in the air.

articleTitle: Negative Influence of Large Static Drives on Industrial Network
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents information on applying the method of theoretical analysis and measurement results on actual static drives and electric network in determining the extent of energetical disturbances and in proposing proper technical measures for adhering to the predetermined limits of individual parameters of quality of the electric power.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Effects on Digital Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The questions of the effects of high frequency EMI on digital ICs of TTL. type were considered.

articleTitle: Optimization of Utilization of Electromagnetic Resources in an Near-Airport Zone via Employing a Joint High-Speed Communication and Navigation System
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Fulfillment of a humanity demand to increase an aircraft freightage leads to an augmentation of intensity of air traffic. Today in an near-large-airport zone intensity of traffic often reaches a critical level. Major part which suffer from informational overload, and which limits airport carrying capacity is a dispatcher service.

articleTitle: A Method of Undesired Signal Registration and Ways of its Realization
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper gives an account of the constructing principle of the device functional circuit for searching and detecting Tinde sired signal sources and explains how it works.

articleTitle: Mathematical Model for Analysis of Electromagnetic Noise Generated by Resistance Welding Machines
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Important features of resistance welding machines are substantial current pulsations in the welding circuit and a highly non-uniform power intake from the supply mains. In order to develop welders that would comply with electromagnetic noise level specifications and be compatible with the supply mains, a careful analysis of higher harmonics generated by resistance welders is therefore essential. With this end in view, a mathematical model was developed which makes it possible to calculate electromagnetic processes and to analyze harmonic composition of currents and voltages in any component of a resistance welder power source. The model was used for the harmonic analysis of the mains current and the welding circuit in application to the thyristor inverter power unit for a steel pipe flash butt welder. The calculations yielded data which permitted selection of appropriate harmonic current suppression devices to be installed at the supply network buses and enabled quantitization of the electromagnetic noise generated by welding current harmonics. The calculated electromagnetic processes in the welding source were corroborated experimentally.

articleTitle: Antenna Structures of Cylindrical Dipoles with Conducting Reflector for Transient Excitation
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transient excitation of thin cylindrical's dipole's structure with conducting reflector is analysed. The transient current and field distributions are obtained by use of direct numerical solution of time-domain electrical field integral formulation for thin conducting cylinders. Two excitation modes are examined - radiation mode, when source is generator; reception mode, when source of excitation is incident field. Transient characteristics of structure are obtained as "smoothed" pulse responsion functions. It is found that the influence on current distribution of conducting reflector's presence at distance h>L/6 is inconsiderable.

articleTitle: Status of the Standardization Work on EMC in IEC, CENELEC and Other Organizations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An intense activity takes place currently in the field of EMC-Standardization. Aim of the report is to give an overview on the present status - beginning 1990 - of the work related to electrical and electronic equipment or systems (EMC-Standardization in other fields like Radiocommunication are in the responsability of other organizations than the ones considered here and are not dealt with). The report gives general information on - the relevant organizations (IEC, CENELEC, etc.) - the disturbance phenomena - the types and subjects of the EMC standards (basic, generic, product related standards) - the status of EMC standardization in IEC (worldwide) - the status of EMC standardization in CENELEC (EMC-Directive of the European Community) - standardization in other organisations - the most important future aspects This information will just describe this general framework. The situation is very different in detail in each organization and changes continously; interested persons should contact the ones they are interested in. Several basic standards exist already or are presently in course of preparation. Generic standards are also in course of preparation. One of the main task for the future will be to work out product related standards.

articleTitle: EMI Radiation on 2.45 GHz
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The work was done in accordance to Res. nr 63 of the WARC 70 allocating new ISM band within 433.05-434.70 MHz, ie. in the centre of intensively exploited communication band. The results of theoretical and practical considerations as well as measurements and observations carried out within 2.45 GHz band are presented. The results are simply transferable to 430 MHz band and show possible interference within communication band caused by ISM. The works conclusion is that it is impossible to accept common band for ISM and communication. ISM should have separate bands and their sporious emmissions should be limited.

articleTitle: Statistical Characteristics of the Radio Signals Propagating along Crossed Paths or in Communication Links
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The statistical characteristics of the coherent signal in the channels with frequency and spatial separation have been investigated. The presence of the turbulent atmosphere influence on the correlation between the signal propagated in the radio channels with spatial separation by crossing of the propagation paths has been confirmed experimentally. The presence of the signal phase fluctuation correlation has been exposed at the 4-11 GHz with frequency separation up to 500 MHz. The results of the experimental estimation of the phase fluctuation dispersion by radio engineering and refractometry measurements are presented. The main consideration is given bo the investigation of the spectral and correlation signal characteristics by the frequency separation.

articleTitle: Type Approval Tests for Radio and Television Receivers According to Italian Regulations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to protect radio communications and broadcast services against radio interference, in 1985 regulations were issued in Italy based on International Standards (CISPR), when available, and on German Standards (DIN-VDE). A radio receiver is at the same time a source of interference and a victim of interference, then emission and immunity measurements are necessary. As far as emission is concerned, the methods of measurement of interference voltages injected into the mains and of radiofrequency voltages present at the antenna, terminals are considered, For the tine being radiation measurements are not mandatory. As regards immunity, two kinds of immunity are considered, the immunity to radiated fields and conducted interference (external immunity), and the immunity to interference caused by broadcast signals on adjacent channels (internal immunity). The various methods of measurement and the relevant limits are shown and the differences compared to CISPR, VDE and CENELEC Standards are indicated.

articleTitle: Regression Model Design for Interference Analysis in Fabric Strip Conductors in Quick Action Equipment
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Constructive and technological peculiarities of fabric strip conductors and appropriateness of their application for quick action radio - electronic equipment is analysed in this paper.

articleTitle: Suppression Technique of Harmonic Interference in Audio Communication
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on the analysis of commercial frequency (50 or 60 HZ) harmonic interference(HI) to the audio communication caused by high voltage transmission line (HVTL), this paper presents the suppression technique of HI. THey are direct methods (including comb filter (CF) method and notch filter (NF) method), voice band compression and shift method and predistortion method. The principles, mathematics models, anti-interference ability and applicable situations are also given in this paper.

articleTitle: Minimization of the Width of the Sanitary Protection Zone (Right-of-Way) of UHV and EHV Electric Power Transmission Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Obtaining of rights of way (ROW) for construction of extra-high voltage (EHV) and ultra-high voltage (UHV) overhead electric power transmission lines (OHL) is becoming more and more of a problem for designers during the recent decade, particularly in densely populated areas. The most urgent goal is to maximize the power transfer capability of lines while minimizing the ROW. This can be done by, among other things, reducing the area of environmental effects of EHV and UHV OHLs, more specifically, through reduction of the width of the sanitary protection zone (SPZ) defined, according to the USSR standards, as the land along a ROW within which the electric field strength at the 1.8 m height above the ground exceeds 1 kV/m<sup>/1/</sup>. It is shown in the paper how the width of the SPZ is affected by facilities used to lower maximum electric field intensity (EFI) and electrostatic induction (ESI) levels on vehicles under OHL conductors<sup>/2,3/</sup> and by other techniques.

articleTitle: Radar Imagery Used for Characterisation of the Interference Due to the Rain Scatter
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Tridimensional reflectivity fields measured by meteorological radars make possible the simulation of virtually any realistic geometry of communication systems affected by the interference due to the rain scatter Radar rain data collected at Spino d'Adda in northern Italy are here used for prediction of coupling between two independent radio systems with typical geometries A simplified version of Bistatic Radar Equation is adopted for the estimation of scattering in terms of joint distribution of the reflectivity inside the common volume and the attenuation along the links. The main goal is to improve the prediction methods for interference parameters in order to reduce the coordination distance of the link, i.e. the area where the strict coordination with neighbouring systems is required.

articleTitle: Environmental Classification and Immunity Test Limits of Electronic Equipment for Professional use in Finland
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is the ability of a device, equipment or system to function satisfactorily in its electromagnetic environment without introducing intolerable disturbances to anything in that environment. Hence, as the first step, environmental conditions must be described. Classification of the electromagnetic environment is going on e.g. in IEC and CENELEC. There are quite many international standards for EMC testing, both emission and immunity, but it is not generally known how environmental classification can be used for different kind of electromagnetic locations. In Finland there is a National SFS Standard of environmental classification and test methods for interference immunity. The values of the environmental parameters are defined according to existing measuring results and experiences. Because the values of the parameters are not always known quantitatively the classification has been made with probabilities.

articleTitle: The Assessment Method for Aeronautical-Broadcast Compatibility Analysis
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the following factors of the assessment method for analysing the interferences to aeronautical stations are presented: compatibility criteria and procedures, mathematical models of system components (FM transmitter, FM antenna, propagation, aircraft antenna system, receiver), test points distribution and the algorithm for compatibility analysis.

articleTitle: The Energy Density Function: A Useful Tool for Solving EMC Problems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The energy content is a very important characteristic for analysing the EMC problems of electrical equipments with electronic unit in case of impulse-like disturbances. The otherwise circuitous and time-waisting calculations can be made easier and by plotting the approximate curve of the energy density function. The simplicity and the benefits of the use of the approximate energy density curve is illustrated by analysing a disturbance coupling problem.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Situation Standard Models for Space-Scattered Sources
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Extensive use of analysis to practically ensure electromagnetic compatibility of radioelectronic devices (EMC RED) stimulates the development of a combination of electromagnetic situation (EMS) standards - pattern probability models of EMS for most common operational conditions of RED. Introduction of such models into scientific and engineering practice is liable to enable an objective and comparative analysis of various technical and organizational variants according to the EMC criteria to be carried out.

articleTitle: Examination of Destabilising Factors Influence on EMI Level, Generated by Regulated Converter, using Pulse-Frequency Modulation
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Regulated converters due to energy parametres transformation and regulation on high-frequency are the class of apparatus with EMI levels more than normative. EMI spectral characteristics depend on converted current and voltage amplitudes, pulses forms and duty ratio. The sources of interference are not only switching semiconductors but also the reactive elements which form the way for unbalanced interference or contour of RFI radiation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transients on Subscriber Lines
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic transients on telecommunication systems may be induced by faults, lightning strikes and switching actions on power systems. This paper presents an alternative simulation technique which can be used in the analysis of electromagnetic transients using a personal computer.

articleTitle: Pulse Signal Propagation at V.H.F Band in Urban Conditions
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: By digital methods of radiosignal transmission the effect of multipath propagation in urban channels of communication is revealed in appearance of delayed impulses leading to distortions of transmitted information. The probablity of appearing such distortions may be evaluated using statistical analysis of parameter changes of pulse signals in various reception conditions typical to a modern city.

articleTitle: LEMP Within the Buildings During a Direct Strikes
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Lightning electromagnetic plus (LEMP) may cause damages or interference in the operation of a majority of electronic and electric systems. For this reason in this paper a theoretical determination of LEMP within the buildings during a direct strikes is presented. These calculations are carried out with a help of a new mathematical function which exactly describes the shape of the lightning current.

articleTitle: Investigations of the Annular Dipole Array for VHF Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In last years wide investigations have been carried out on the application of local VHF hypertheraia for the cancer therapy. An urgent problem of modern VHF hypertheraia is to ensure deep local heating of tumours.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency EMC in Low Voltage Power Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An overview is given on the standardization progress related to low-frequency disturbances on power supply systems, considering the following aspects: compatibility levels, emission levels, immunity tests and measurement methods.

articleTitle: A Simulator of Conductive Pulse Interference
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper some problems of simulation methods and realisation of a conductive pulse simulator are considered. The simulator generates pulse sequences and random power pulses with characteristics specified by a user. The appliance is intended for investigations directed to the determination of immunity of the equipment under test (EUT) in relation to various types of pulse interference in supply circuits either of the determinate or random character.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation Spectrum Emitted by a Positive Corona Discharge D.C. Source Supplied
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work the results of measurements of the frequency characteristics of the electric and magnetic components of the electromagnetic interference field generated by various forms of the positive corona discharge (a filmy corona, a brush corona, a bridged-streamer corona) and the mixed discharge composed of the bridged-streamer corona and the glow discharge are presented. The discharges studied operated in the air or in the 16% CO<inf>2</inf>/N<inf>2</inf> mixture (a simulator of exhaust gases) under the atmospheric pressure between a single needle electrode or a set of 7 needle electrodes {polarized positively) and a plate electrode polarized negatively. The discharge was supplied from a d.c. source. The results obtained show that in the case of using the needle electrode with a relatively large curvature of its rounded cone top the electromagnetic interference is higher than that generated when the needle with a small top curvature is used. The frequency spectra of the electromagnetic interference generated by the positive corona discharge and the mixed discharge range from about 0.01 MHz to several MHz for the electric component, and from about 0.1 MHz to several MHz for the magnetic one. The intensity of the electric component is higher than that of the magnetic one regardless of the form of the discharge. Comparing various forms of the positive corona discharge, the lowest electromagnetic interference is generated by the filmy corona, while the highest by the bridged-streamer corona. The positive corona in the 16 % CO<inf>2</inf>/N<inf>2</inf> mixture emits the interference of higher intensity than that produced by the discharge in the air. This is to be taken into account if practical applications of a positive corona discharge to purification of exhaust gases is considered. Comparison shows that the electromagnetic interference generated by the positive corona discharge is several times higher than that generated by the negative corona discharge at similar conditions. This is of importance if the electromagnetic interference compatibility aspect of practical applicability of both discharges must be taken into account.

articleTitle: Buried and Shielded Cable Response to a Subsequent Return Stroke
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of the proposed paper is to present an analysis of the lightning induced disturbances affecting the performance of communication and electronic devices linked by buried and shielded cables. A comparison between predicted and experimental results is presented. Furthermore some numerical examples are given in the form of a parametric analysis.

articleTitle: Applicability of Engineering Models in Frequency Planning
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Spectrum management process involves a large number of tasks, of both administrative and technical nature. One of the most creative activities is the frequency planning. In this paper the frequency planning is dealt from the standpoint of its following features: - Interference analysis of radiocommunication network - Assignment of a new frequency within existing network - Design of a network using exclusively new assignments - Performance estimation of a proposed network Solving all problems is usually achieved with the help of modelling and simulation methods based on engineering models in connection with measurements results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field inside Loaded TEM Cells
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a brief review of Methods which are used in theoretical analysis of Crawford cells. A generalised numerical Method using the Method of Moments is applied to evaluate the field pattern and the characteristic impedance of loaded cells with objects of any shape. Results for rectangular cylinders are presented.

articleTitle: Generation Mechanism and Properties of Noise Induced by Relays Switching
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An electromagnetic relay generates electrical noise accompanied with discharge. This noise causes malfunction in digital circuit. Characteristic of TTL IC's malfunction due to the noise source is as follows: the rate of malfunction decreases with increasing the relay circuit current. The mechanisms of the characteristic are discussed in detail by measuring the induced noise and by the occurrence causes of each discharge mode on the break of contacts.

articleTitle: Optimization of Wide-Range Antennas with Loads
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Linear large length vibrator with concentrated loads that in wide frequency range ensures high level of matching with cable and radiation maximum in the plane, perpendicular to the vibrator axis, is considered in the authors' article published in Proceeding of international Wroclaw simposium on Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC-88).

articleTitle: Test-Based Statistical Data on Characteristics of Microgap Discharges
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic radiation at frequencies from those below the radio broadcast band to those above the range of television channels may result from microgap discharges that could occur on inadequately designed and poorly maintained power lines. Elimination of electromagnetic interference often means additional cost, to the operating utility. Detailed information at the design stage on case and characteristics of microgap discharges should help to lower the probability of their occurrance and thus reduce the maintenance cost. Studies made under laboratory conditions to date indicate that waveshape of microgap discharge currents and the corresponding frequency spectra are statistical in nature. Their exact statistical characterization depends on the detailed gap geometry and is also a function of the potential difference between the two electrodes. In addition, these two factors determine whether the discharge form is indeed a microgap discharge or actually a corona discharge. Transition from microgap to corona discharge is found to be gradual rather than abrupt. The paper explores in detail the nature and statistical transition region.

articleTitle: The Changing World of Telecommunication: Standardization in a Rapidly Changing Environment as a Challenge for CCITT
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At no other time in its 125 years' history the ITU been more challenged than is presently the case. Its two standardization bodies, CCITT and CCIR, are in the forefront of developing global standards, tieing together the more and more complicated, ever-increasing world-wide web of telecommunications. Standardization of ISDN is just one example of how ITU has successfully managed its task as a global standardization authority - but much more remains to be done. Standardization in the competitive environment, as it exists today, is certainly not a foolproof job; different interests of competing organizations and companies, which should be brought to a consensus, should be kept in mind - an undertaking that might sometimes even fail. Fortunately, all the parties concerned are now increasingly aware of the fact that, by the end of the day, a standard is beneficial to all of them, whereas no standard at all would be detrimental.

articleTitle: Testing of Susceptibility and Vulnerability - Waveforms Used for
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper waveforms of voltage, current and electromagnetic field used for testing of susceptibility and vulnerability of electrical/electronic equipment are reviewed. The waveforms are described analytically, graphically or by specification of their main parameters. Three classes of waveforms are distinguished: double exponential, double exponential derivative, dumped oscillatory (sinusoid or cosinusoid). A great number and variety of the waveforms required by different compulsory standards is pointed out and discussed.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Pulses of the Natural Field of the Earth on Low Frequencies
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A number of published papers show that intensive earthquakes may be Preceded by electromagnetic precursors having the form of anomalous variation of the natural random field of the Earth of an atmospheric-electrical nature. Particularly it has been Observed on low frequencies (LF) around 80 kHz. One hypothesis about the possible origin of electromagnetic precursor of the earthquakes is a subsurface impulsive radiation at the preparation area of the earthquake due to various mechanoelectrical effects. Investigations related to studies of LF electromagnetic earthquake precursors attract increased attention to studies of natural variation of the fields of the Earth in this frequency band, since in the long run detection of field anomalies demands detailed knowledge of this fiels as radio-noise forming the background for the effects to be detected. One possible way in developing the methods to estimate the anomalous natural field variation due to the earthquake precursor may be the quantitative estimation of changes of statistical properties of the field. This requires detailed knowledge of variation of the field model parameters. The present report uses a working statistical model of the field being presented in the form of random atmospheric pulses sequence described by previously developed dependence of pulse flow intensity ν(s<sup>−1</sup>) versus the threshold field E(mkV/m):

articleTitle: Radiative Emission of Microwaves from Biological Media
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Assuming a three layer model living tissues. the reflectivity and brightness temperature has been computed as a function of look angle. polarization and varying thickness of the layer at three microwave frequencies. A new effort has been made to explain the abrupt changes in brightness temperature. This may be due to presence of some non-absorbing medium as a result of abnormal growth of tissues. because more absorption will give rise to more emission. In last. an inversion technique using Kalman filtering algorithms has been suggested to extract the real temperature of the parts of the body in layered media using the remotely sensed temperature from various parts of the body.

articleTitle: Algorithmic Support and Software of Large Dimension Frequency Planning Tasks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The solution of frequency planning tasks for non-regular radio networks (broadcasting, mobile communication) is a sequence of compromises between contradictory requirements to a computer memory, internal performance and accuracy.

articleTitle: Effective Resistive-Capacitive Elements of Broadband Interference Suppressing Filters
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using of rational design of a resistive-capacitive element of multilayer structure is considered for creation of effective interference suppressing filters in the frequency range 100kHz-10GHz. A sufficiently accurate method of power attenuation of such elements is proposed which is at the same time acceptable for engineering practice. Additional requirements to self ohmic losses are determined. High technical characteristics of multilayer resisteve-capacitive elements (RCE) permit to use them as independent filtering appliances.

articleTitle: Plasma Chemical Vapor Deposition and its Application to Amorphous Semiconductor Devices
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Plasma Chemical Vapor Deposition (CVD) is widely used for fabricating semiconductor devices such as LSI's and amorphous silicon (a-Si) devices. In this paper, we review our recent studies of plasma CVD technology in which microwave discharges and pulse discharges are applied, with a view to understand the role of discharge plasma in the film deposition processes. The present status of a-Si devices developed in our laboratory is also presented.

articleTitle: Radiation and Reception on Non-Sinusoidal Disturbances
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of radiating the disturbance by the sources with the non-sinusoidal current - lightning discharge, sparking, etc. - is considered on the basis of the vector potential method. The time-domain approach is used for calculating the disturbance fields. The problem of the non-sinusoidal disturbance reception is solved by means of the integral equations derived from the boundary conditions for the vector potential. The problem of the relationship between the transmission and reception characteristics is considered. A new formula for estimating the Induced power is suggested, the induced vector potential as well as the current being used here. On the basis of the formula mentioned, the equation for the reciprocity coefficient between the disturbance source and receiver is obtained.

articleTitle: Immunity of FM Receivers Against Impulsive Interference
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the problem of the immunity measurements of FM receivers' against impulsive interference. Two methods of measurements and appropriate resuits for vehicle and home receivers are discussed. The need of IEC method modification is suggested.

articleTitle: Quantification of the EMC Properties of Automated Devices
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the recent 30 years a lot of electronic devices, equipment and systems were introduced into the plant floor to control machines or processes, where they usually have to work under very harsh electromagnetic environmental conditions. The EMC related design and evaluation of such an equipment requires a quantitative description of the EMC features. The aim of the present paper is to show how the EMC-qualities of automatic devices and systems can be described quantitatively in accordance to the well known definition of the term EMC in the IEV and in conformity to corresponding national and international specifications.

articleTitle: Electric Discharge in Breaking Contacts
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric discharge in breaking contacts as a noise source is discussed. Arc discharges occur at an instant of contact break, and the arc type is different from each other for load condition; continuous arc for resistive load and intermittent arc (showering arc) for inductive load. The phenomena of those arcs are analyzed from both measuring and statistical point of view.

articleTitle: Generalized Characteristics of Current Probe in Non-Quasistationary Mode
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analisis is given of a more correct model of the shielded Rogowsky coil - the current probe, which at high frequencies is a chain with distributed parameters and a distributed source of emf. The equations that describe processes in the line are solved with due account of the current probe working conditions in the current transformation mode. The expression is obtained for transformation coefficient in a non-quasistationary mode, on the basis of which the transition is done to one of the main characteristics of the current probe - the transition conductivity. The change of the transition conductivity value normalized to the wave resistance of the coil makes it possible to express it in the form determined only by coil parameters. On the basis of the calculations proposed the signals are singled out which make it possible to explain the changes taking place in the coil of the current probe as a result of a standing wave formed in it and it is shown that the fully matched mode is impossible to obtain. A good agreement of the calculation results with experimental studies is registered.

articleTitle: The Changing World of Radiocommunication
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: High capacity digital radio-relay and satellite systems are developing to support the whole range of digital video and data services of ISDN's. Modern radio-relay and satellite links, many employing small aperture antennas, offer important options to optical fibre in many geographical and economic situations. New mobile radio offers data, facsimile, and voice. More than any other radio service, future universal personal mobile communications in the world network will depend on standards and spectrum. Broadcasting is advancing to high-definition television, and possibly digital satellite sound. Other new space services afford greater maritime and aeronautical safety and efficiency, more accurate navigation, meteorological observation and space research.

articleTitle: The IFRB Frequency Management System the Growing Role of Computer Databases in Planning and Coordination of the Radio Frequency Spectrum and the Geostationary Satellite Orbit
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Introduction of new radio stations and replacement of old services by new ones needs planning and coordination, nationally and internationally, which is becoming more complex with Increased congestion of the spectrum and the orbit, and due to changing pattern of user services.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) Generated by Plasma Accelerators
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Noise properties of the plasma accelerator (PA) were considered on the basis of presenting it as a model comprising of a number of interconnected member. The paper describes the characteristics of fluctuations in power supply system (PSS) and plasma jet, distinguished were the methods of monitoring thereof and determined were the factors exerting Influence on the EM level.

articleTitle: The Changing World of Telecommunications - Standardization in a Rapidly Changing Environment as a Challenge for CCITT
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: At no other time in its 125 years' history has the ITU been more challenged than is presently the case. Its two standardization bodies, CCITT and CCIR, are in the forefront of developing global standards, tieing together the more and more complicated, ever-increasing world-wide web of telecommunications. Standardization of ISDN is just one example of how ITU has successfully managed its task as a global standardization authority - but much more remains to be done. Standardization in the competitive environment, as it exists today, is certainly not a foolproof job; different interests of competing organizations and companies, which should be brought to a consensus, should be kept in mind - an undertaking that might sometimes even fail. Fortunately, all the parties concerned are now increasingly aware of the fact that, by the end of the day, a standard is beneficial to all of them, whereas no standard at all would be detrimental.

articleTitle: Prediction and Measurement of Electromagnetic Field, Penetrating Through the Aperture into Conducting Screen
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analytical expressions for the electric (&) and magnetic (&) fields induced by the thunder-storm discharge, which penetrate through the elliptical aperture in a conducting screen were obtained by the method of the variables subdivision within the ellipsoidal coordinate system. The computation error of these fields has been determined through the use of equivalent electric and magnetic dipoles. The method of the measurement error estimation by the capasitive transduser of the finite dimensions in the non-uniform electrical field has been developed by the combination of the integral equation method with the Greenberg theorem on induced potentials. The relationship between the dimensions of the transduser and aperture which provides the specified level of the measurement error has been determined.

articleTitle: A Universal Simulator of Sources of Strong Electromagnetic Fields Intended for Studying the Sensitivity of Electronic Equipment to Such Fields
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The structure of a simulator of sources of strong electromagnetic fields is being examined, which makes the radiators of electric and magnetic fields interrelated but synchronized. The structure is constructed with the help of the Helmholtz coils and capacitance electrodes with a guard ring, which are placed in the planes at right angles to each other with a common symmetry centre, the coils being connected with the current generator, and the electrodes with the voltage generator. Both generators are constructed by using the same circuit design on the basis of a two-stroke inductive batcher with regeneration of the residual energy. In contrast with the simulator based on the TEM-chamber, the suggested simulator is much more universal in respect of frequency ranges, correlations, between the amplitudes of field components, and the forms of pulse disturbances. The test chamber of the suggested simulator is one third as large as the TEM-chamber. The simulator is provided with magneto and electrometric sensors.

articleTitle: Acceleration of Discharge Formation Caused by a Fast Approach of Electrode and the Over-Voltage
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It has been observed that a rising slope of current waveform of an air gap discharge is influenced by an approaching speed of electrodes. The effects of fast approach of electrodes upon the discharge formation are discussed based on the over-voltage defined by the Paschen's law.

articleTitle: Refractive Characteristics of the Atmosphere in the Far-Eastern Regions of the USSR
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The necessity of providing E.M.C. with radioelectronic means different physico - climatic conditions of the globe demands scrupylous study of radiometeorological parameters of atmosphere. It concerns also vast territories of the Pacific Ocean's coast scantily explored from this point of view.

articleTitle: Frequency Correlation of Millimeter Radiation in Precipitations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental studies of frequency correlation function of millimeter wave band fluctuations in precipitations are represented. A theoretical analysis of mutual statistic moments of two frequency-separated signals has been made on the basis of the multiple scattering first approximation theory. The effect of scatterer nonsphericity of hydrometeors has been studied. Numerical calculations analysis has revealed that in the case of antennas usually used in millimeter band and practically interesting near-earth paths the particle shape produces greater effect in the long-wave part of the band. The maximum values <tex>$\Delta_{j}= (6_j^2-6_o^2)/6_o^2$</tex>, where <tex>$6_o^2(f)$</tex> and <tex>$6_o^2(f)$</tex> are field variances in case of spherical and nonspherical particles and "j" is radiation polarisation index, take place for the vertical polarization of antennas in the case of identically oriented particles, when their symmetry axes coinside vertically. For the rain rate I = 25mm/h at frequency f = 30GHz the value is |Δ<inf>v</inf>| =26%. At increased variance of paticle canting angles the magnitude is reduced. In nature there exist many causes resulting the deflection of symmetry axis from vertical direction therefore the identical orientation of particles can be considered as the maximum possible case. Theoretical investigation of frequency correlation function has been carried out for spherical particles. Calculation results analysis showed that the correlation bandwidth is reduced as the path length becomes longer. When converting into the short-wave part of millimeter band the magnitude is increased. In the case when narrow pattern antennas are used, the correlation coefficient is slightly dependent on precipitation rate. The rain rate growth results in variance increase. Calculations revealed that the derectional characteristics of antennas greatly affect on frequency correlation. Increase in aperture size leads to significant broadening of the correlation bandwidth. The experimental investigations of mutual correlation of two signals with 6,8-7,8GHz carried frequency difference have been carried out on the near-earth 4-km line-of-sight in the long-wave part of millimeter band. Antennas with <tex>$1^{\circ}$</tex> lobe width have been used in measurements. The obtained data agree satisfactorily with the results of calculations.

articleTitle: Tracking Wide Band Signals Radio Receivers Noise Immunity with Additive Frequency Modulation in the Case of Carrier Frequency Modulated by Information Communication
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Calculation relationships for tracking wide band signals radio receivers noise immunity with additive frequency modulation before the detector in the canals with frequency concentrated noises have been got.

articleTitle: Transmission-Line Matrix Modelling of Wide-Band Absorbing Surfaces
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A novel type of an E-M wave absorber is presented. The absorber consists of a thin ferrite layer and a biasing circuit. The ferrite is magnetized by the biasing circuit, thus adjusting the resonant absorption to the frequency of the E-M field. This feature allows wide-band performance of such absorber. The absorbing properties of the structure are simulated by Transmission-Line Matrix method. The results of this simulation demonstrate clearly the superiority of presented structure if compared with standard thin-coating ferrite absorber. The manufacturing method by APS-technique is finally discussed.

articleTitle: A Questionnaire Survey of Electromagnetic Interference in Spanish Hospitals
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We report the results of a questionnaire survey of electromagnetic interference in Spanish hospitals. We consider that our findings should be borne in mind both when new electronic equipment is installed in existing hospitals and in the desing and siting of new centers. Research in this field should lead to improved standars for hospital equipment and the introduction of relevant legal provisions.

articleTitle: The Changing World of Radio Communications Spectrom and Future Radio
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The future of many new telecommunication services depends on availability of frequency spectrum. Suitable bands are largely already in use. New strategies and techniques are needed for more intensive shared use of the spectrum resource. A World Administrative Radio Conference will be held in 1992 to deal with frequency allocations in certain parts of the spectrum. Re-allocation in the frequency range 1 to 3 GHz will be considered to provide spectrum for mobile-satellite and other mobile services, satellite HDTV and possibly satellite sound broadcasting, and possible extension of bands for HF broadcasting will be considered. An ITU Group of Experts will also in the near future study possible new frequency allocation methods and radio regulations, to allow more possibilities for services and frequency sharing.

articleTitle: Two-Winding Coil in Current Probe
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A constructive realization of the current probe coil in the form of a many-way helicon coil forming separate chains not connected with each other is proposed. The simplest variant of the constructive realization is considered - a two-winding coil in a current probe. On the basis of analysis of its work in non-quasistationaxy condition it is shown that such construction leads to decreasing of the coil secondary parameter value - the propagation constant, which determines fully one of the main characteristics of the coil - the transition conductivity. The estimation is given of the possibility of increasing the upper limiting frequency of the two-winding coil construction in comparison with a conventional one, containing one coil. This estimation is based on the analysis of the values of the propagation constants of the long lines formed by the coils and the shielding case and between each other. It was concluded that effects existing between the coils of the current probes does not allow to realize fully the possibilities of the two-winding coil as far as rising of upper limit of frequency is concerned.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Emissions in Upper Ionosphere Over Earthquake Areas Aboard Two Satellites Data
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A wide varlaty of publikations on observation of electromagnetic emissions in the frequency range 10<sup>2</sup> + 10<sup>4</sup> Hz close to the seismic centre /1, 2/ and above centres /3-11/ appeared for the past few years. Investigations of electromagnetic emissions above the supposed seismic centre, in the upper ionosphere on two satellites are of great importance for understanding of meachanizm for emergence of low frequency emissions.

articleTitle: Methods of Electromagnetic Interference Conseliation for Power Widebend High Frequency Units
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the major sources of electromagnetic interferences (EMI) is a radio transmitter that requires developing spesial means for reduction of its unwanted radiation. The problem becomes guite a complex one when stages of radiotransmitters are wide band amplifiers with bandwidth of several octaves and tuning or switching selective power circuits are not feasible.

articleTitle: The Modern Trends in Radio Spectrum Management and EMC of Radio Systems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The main problems in radio spectrum management and EMC of radio means are solved by realization of a complex of technical and organizational measures. Technical measures resolve themself into perfection of parameters and technical haracteristics of apparatus EMC. Organizational measures include distribution, frequency assignment and allocation for radio networks and radio services, determination of frequency, space and time separations of radio stations and other measures influencing EMC of large groups of radio means. Realization of the above is connected with the need for storage of great amount of formation, simulating of hard EM environment and labour consuming calculations of interference levels in reception channels. By this reason they may be realised only with a help of automated systems of radiospectrum management using fast-response computers with large volume of operational and external memory. Technological principles of radio-spectrum management include some international and national aspects. International spectrum management is based on decisions and recommendations of international organizations (CCIR, IEC and so on). National problems of spectrum management are solved for large regions (including territory of the whole country), specified territorial areas and isolated objects (radio communication units, ships, aircrafts and so on). In the USSR a member of automated systems for analysis and prediction of radio means EMC, establishing limits of frequency-space separation and frequency planning of radio networks. In the paper a description of automated systems of radio spectrum management in the USSR is presented, solved problems are considend and main technical characteristics are given, including an operalional system, programm language and a control system for data lases.

articleTitle: Frequency Planning in Mobile Radio Networks
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The frequency assignment problem in mobile radio networks and frequency-distance constraints (FDC) determination problem are analyzed. Different methods for mutual interference prediction are observed together with the possibility for FDC calculation they give. Special emphasis is laid on a new method for FDC acquisition, combined with a feasible heuristic method for frequency assignment. The substantiated new ideas give the chance to take into account multiple interference, instead of only base station (BS) to base station mutual interference.

articleTitle: New Non Thermal Bio Effect to Eyes on EMC in Amature Radio
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For long while, we believed that the human eyes were damaged as the cataract of crystalline lens of eyes by affect of thermal heating of the electromagnetic wave energy which radiated from an antenna and an ungrounded case panel of the radio equipments. The worst case of this effect is usual y explained to the walkie-talkie with higher powered transmitter, when the operator keeps the antenna of these equipments just close his face. Since 1985, a Canadian medical doctor Dr. Kues and et. al were discovered a more dangerous effect on human eye destroyed of their corneal endothelium by the non thermal effect of electromagnetic energy. In this case, the dangerous damage was appeared at only 5 - 10% of the total power density of the case of thermal effect in the same conditions. The author will present this new dangerous campane on EMC in this paper.

articleTitle: Energetic Electronic Devices of Pulse-Modulation Type with Hightened Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Energy and information electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of energy electronics is considered, An universal structure of an pulse-modulation converter with multizone pulse modulation (MPM) is proposed. Multizone pulse modulation decreases immediate-action commutation power and improves energy and information EMC. Double modulation of an energy flux in the universal structure increases energy EMC of the converter with mains supply and provides sinusoidal current from mains supply. Theoretical and experimental researches of the universal structure are considered.

articleTitle: Acoustic Detection of Millimeter Wavelength Radiation Power Absorbed by Biological Objects
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The method of acoustic detection of absorbed power (ADAP) of millimeter (MM) waves is proposed. The present work presents data on the frequency dependence of MM wave power absorbtion in water solutions obtained using ADAP. An installation is described that realises two versions of the method, one of them being microphone chamber and the other based on the registration of acoustic signal in the object itself.

articleTitle: The Measurement of the Frequency Dependence of Ionospheric Exit Points and Polarization of Low-Latitude Whistlers
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new method of wide-band direction finding for whistlers, based on the simultaneous measurement of two horizontal magnetic field components and one vertical electric field component using the digital recorders and a fast Fourier transform analyser, has carried out for daytime whistlers at low latitude Yamaoka (geomag. lat. 25°N). It is found that there is a negligibly small frequency dependence of the ionospheric exit point and polarization of daytime whistlers during each occurrence peak with duration of about 2 hours, which lends further support to their propagation in field-aligned duct In the magnetosphere for each occurrence peak.

articleTitle: On-Vehicle Data Busses - Mobile Radio Effects
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper includes the presentation of results of tests undertaken to determine typical EMC stresses on vehicle mounted electronics when mobile radio is operated on a vehicle which is fitted with a data bus. With the increased use of both mobile radio and electronic data paths on vehicles used in the public sector this aspect of EMC is becoming more important as time passes.

articleTitle: Wroclaw Electromagnetic Pulse Laboratory
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Wrocław Electromagnetic Pulse Threat Laboratory (WEMPTL) equipped with various system for BMP susceptibility testing is presented. Methods of succeptibility testing can be divided into two major classes: field simulation and injection. In the injection method, a pulse generator is connected directly to the input terminals of the object under test. The pulse generator simulates EMP-induced currents and voltages that will be picked up by a feeder, cable or circuit. In the field simulation method, the pulse generator is connected to an EMP simulator. The electromagnetic environment produced should be as close as possible to the actual threat.

articleTitle: System Modeling of Electrostatic Discharge Waveforms
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electrostatic discharge waveforms measured under different conditions and reported in the literature are digitized and stored in a computer. They are modeled as the impulse response of a linear discrete system. The coefficients of the corresponding system function are identified and the model output is compared to the measured ESD signal. It is shown that the model adequately represents the ESD pulses. The knowledge of the system function corresponding to the ESD waveform will permit the synthesis of circuits which can reproduce the waveform. This can, in term, lead to the design and implementation of ESD simulators which can generate the pulses discharged from various discharging objects and occurring under different test conditions.

articleTitle: Prediction of Spectral Composition of Interference Voltage in Transistor Converters
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the work presented here methods of predicting voltage of symmetric and asymmetric interference generated by the units provided with transistor converters are suggested. The methods are based on singling out the active and passive sources in the converter circuit that generate interference voltage the spectral composition of which is determined by the switching linearized processes. The interference from each source is spreaded to the receiver by the circuits formed by the parasitic parameters of the unit circuit elements and it causes the introduction of the highfrequency equivalent circuits being in the set a mathematic model of processes of generating interference by the converter. The resulting influence of all the sources is established by taking into account the phase relations of voltage generated by the given sources. The methods allow to predict the levels and spectral composition of the interference voltage considering practically all the factors that determine it.

articleTitle: The Synthesis of Long and Medium Wave Directional Antenna Arrays: A Microcomputer-Based Approach
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Several mathematical approaches have been proposed to synthesize antenna patterns. These methods show various degrees of performance and difficulty in their implementation in a personal computer environment.

articleTitle: Frequency Planning - The Basic Element of Spectrum Management
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This is an introductory paper to the Invited Special Section of the Symposium. The part played by frequency planning in measures aimed at the efficient spectrum management is determined. The paper considers the basic stages in frequency planning - from the most general problems of frequency band allocations to different radio services up to specific problems of establishing frequency-territory plans for particular services in the given areas. Issues analyzed in other papers on the subject to be presented at the Symposium are also covered. Some general problems on frequency sharing and its effect on frequency planning of particular radio services are given at length in the Annex.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Radio Emissions from Geostationary Satellites at Small Monitoring Stations
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The scope for the use of small monitoring earth stations to evaluate the actual efficiency of frequency assignments to satellite communication systems and to examine emission of geostationary satellites in different frequency band is considered. The structure of a monitoring earth station is discribed, its technical characteristics and parameters to be measured are given. The advantages of monitoring earth stations having a reduced figure-of-merit are shown.

articleTitle: Measures to Ensure the Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) in Automotive Electronics
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing application of electronic devices in motor vehicles necessitates particular measures to guarantee the electromagnetic compatibility. They can be carried out at the interference source, transmission path or interference drain: - Interference Source: Limitation of the interference generation (reduction of the interference emission) - Transmission path: Limitation of the interference transmissions - Interference drain: Limitation of the interference effects (increase of the interference immunity) The following measures are possible for these three objects: assembly, separation, filtering, earthing, screening and arrangements over operation runs. Transposition and mode of transmission can be additionally used for the transmission path.

articleTitle: Prediction and Analysis of Electromagnetic Radiations of TWT
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Possibilities of prediction of side and out-of-band TWT radiations by means of a developed system of automated design of the interaction space have been considered. Main principles of non-linear wave theory assumed as a basis of simulation program of multi-frequency processes in TWT are given. The comparison of results of numerical analysis of side and out-of-band oscillation spectra with experiment has been accomplished. A simple technique of plotting the limitation line of the out-ofband oscillation spectrum with pulse modulation which takes into account phase carrier modulation is offered.

articleTitle: Summary of Paper Interference Immunity of Radio-Teletype Systems in Maritime Communications
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In accordance with IMO's decision all maritime radio communications which use Morse code audio reception will have been replaced by radioteletype (RATT) by 1992. That's why researches in field of interference immunity of radioteletype equipment with different types of code and modulation used are of particular concern.

articleTitle: Analysis of Methods for Channel Quality Control
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper contains the estimation of the quality of radio channels of cellular mobile systems, it elaborates a method for channel quality control for the digital transmission of signals taking into account a preset estimation reliability. Characteristics are obtained which make it possible to determine an optimal analysis period as a function of preset system parameter values.

articleTitle: Distribution of Electromagnetic Field from External and Internal Sources in Dwelling House
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the article the methods of measuring the transfer coefficient, the summarisation of the results of measurements concerning various sources which cause electromagnetic fields inside the building are described. Following problems are dealt with: - the simulation of tram disturbances in narrow streets (0,2 + 180 MHz) - the penetration of external fields into dwelling panel house (0,2 + 23 MHz) - the penetration of fields radiated from building wiring, into one socket of which HF energy is injected, into a dwelling panel house The results are presented in the form of tables and graphs.

articleTitle: Automation of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) Radio Electronic Devices (RED) Characteristics Control by A Two-Frequency Probing (TFP) Method
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A two-frequency probing method (TFP) refers to the most informative and productive methods of EMC RED characteristics control. Its application during different stages of RED life cycle essentialy increases the prediction possibility of radio interference and EMC insurance in various conditions of exploitation.

articleTitle: Household T V-Receiver Susceptibility to the Interfering Signals in a Wide Frequency Range
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The procedure and results of measurments of the internal SECAM TV receiver video channel susceptibility in the VHP range are presented in the report. There was investigated the susceptibility to interferencias refer to three different types: off-channel (at the neigbouring frequences), spurious and intermodulation.

articleTitle: Blocking the Receiver by Mutual Pulse Interference Stream
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on the concept of mean transconductance or active circuit component or radiofrequency amplifier the notion or mean transconductance statistically averaged over a stream of pulse interference (PI) is introduced. Statistically averaged mean transconductance obtained by means of stochastic pulse streams theory is a function or active circuit component transconductance at the initial point of operating duty, the probability of coincidence of signal stream and PI, mean signal pulses duration and mean duration of coincidence stream pulses. The degree of PI blocking of radio receiving device (RRD), equipped with some interference protectors, is determined.

articleTitle: Adaptive Approach to Pulse Interference Cancellation in Modulation Radiometry
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Theoretical evaluation of errors in radiometrical measurements against the background of pulse interference is carried out. The results of quasioptimal algorithms efficiency analysis in processing radiometrical signals when affected by pulse interference streams are presented. Nonlinear, nonlinear-parametric and adaptive methods of interference cancellation are considered. Results of imitation simulation and experimental data confirming the considered algorithms' high efficiency are given.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Responsible Microelectronic Traffic Control Systems
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is the most acute in microelectronic control systems connected with the safety of railway traffic. To solve the problem of the EMC a norm-rated concept is suggested which is based on the notions of "norm" and "standard" and which includes the routine of calculations of disturbance protection means for a specific electromagnetic situati on(EMS) and methods of testing the objects. The equipment for measuring the parameters of disturbances and carrying out tests includes various measuring instruments and disturbance simulators communicating with a microcomputer via IEEE-488 interface.

articleTitle: On the Generation of Electrotelluric Fields by Crustal Geodynamic Processes
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper is concerned with the generation of electrotelluric fields (ETF) by crustal geodynamic processes. It is hypothesized that crustal deformation. excites ETF because of the electrokinetic effect. Based on this model, we propose a new technique for measuring ETF, different from the conventional methods. We discuss the results of simultaneous measurements at a site for ETF (with the new technicue) and land tilts. A good correlation is established between the variations of tilt and ETF for periods of a few days. It is concluded that a network of observation sites can be used to study the spatiotemporal distribution of crustal strain.

articleTitle: Set of Probes for Measuring Pulsing and Continuous Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Measures to establish electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of radioelectronic means nvolves experimental assessment of magnetic fields. To shape the electromagnetic environment the power and frequency radiated fields, environmental situation and distance from the sources of radiation and various sources of magnetic fields should be taken into account. The complexity and variability of such compatibility require the development of methods and means for measuring it. Here we summarize the results of development of various probes for measuring the magnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Recent Results of Studies of Distributions of Extreme Values of the Radio Refractive Index
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Recent results of studies of the long term distribution of radio refractive index profiles in the coastal zone in the notrh of Poland are presented. Distributions of extreme values of the radio refractive index in the first 100 m near-the-ground layer of the troposphere and its gradient were examined. The usefullness of two models of distributions of extreme values were investigated, too.

articleTitle: Overview of Spectrum Managmeent Practices Today and in the Future
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This report examines the necessary technical bases to facilitate the introduction of computer aided Spectrum Management procedures, the development of recommended interference analysis techniques and the development of an agreed format for the exchange of computer generated coordination information A Handbook describing procedures to accomplish these functions has been completed by the CCIR. This report also gives an overview of spectrum management practices today and in the future based on experience gained from the development of the CCIR handbook and the results of additional experience by the United States and other countries in automating national spectrum management systems.

articleTitle: Quasicoherent Reception of Discrete-Continuous Signals Under the Inflience of Intense Non-Gausian Interference
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the information transmission systems and circuits the signal reception and processing is accompanied by intensive interference due to the influence of outside radiodevices. Statistic characteristics of such interference differ from Gausian one. The problem of synthesis and analysis of optimal and quasioptimal receivers arises taking into account the influence of electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Interactive System of Switch-Mode Power Supply RFI-Filters
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Switch-mode power supply RFI-filters design is a complicated process which can't be formalized severely. because of great variety factors influenced on filters attenuation: charactor and meanings of EMI sources and receptors resistances; filter elements types; SMPS, RFI-filter and energy receiver variants of connection and grounding etc.

articleTitle: Transient Disturbance Types and Cases in the Power Distribution Network of Civil Buildings
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The importance of the transient disturbances superimposed upon the power-mains voltage is analyzed and discussed in the light of the existing literature and of the Authors' experimental results. Several typical transients have been measured using especially developed broadband voltage probes with power-mains suppression and flat frequency response (amplitude and phase). The origin of the typical transients is analyzed and discussed from the point of view of their common- or differential mode nature, in relation to the generation mechanism and the frequency range, for what can be expected to occur in a building for civil use.

articleTitle: Calculation of Industrial Electromagnetic Interference in Inner Ship Compartments
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Modern ships are highly saturated by electronic systems. A significant part of these systems uses information in a sound frequency range (up to 20 KHz). Therefore to develop requirements on interference resistance for these sistems. it is necessary to predict electromagnetic environment and in particular, electromagnetic field levels in ship compartments at the locations of electronic system sensors.

articleTitle: Method of the Formation of the Band Signal with the Continuous Spectrum
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The method of the formation of test Interference signal for analysis of various electronic circuits and systems, basing on the dynamical stohasticity phenomenon is suggested. The simple finite-dimensional oscillating system model generating the complicate noise-like signal in the desirable freqwency band is considered. The bifurcation regularities leading to arising chaotic oscillations are studied. The possibility of the signal structure control and freqwency band properties are shown. The experimental sample dynamic is discussed.

articleTitle: Model of Rail Current on Electrification Railway
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The traction network is a strong current, unbalanced. nonlinear, multi-conductor, time-varying distributed parameter system. The rails are under such a sophisticated electromagnetic field. The model of the rails current cannot be created very well only by conventional transmission line theory. Based on the Maxwell equation, the authors regard the model from the view of both field and circuit and then put forward the mathematical mode! The earth effect is considered. The model can be applied to not only homogeneous earth but also multi-layer earth. In addition, many factors are taken into consideration. For instance, the resistive, inductive and capacitive coupling, the earth potential and the frequency response of the traction system. Such parameters as the earth conductivity and the ballast resistance were tested on the railway side. Finally, the authors solved the model in digital computer and analyses the error. The test equipments of the strong current were developed successfully by our research group at the department of Comm. and Control in Northern Jiaotong University. We used the test equipments to have made an experiment on the railway spot. The results of the theoretical analysis turn out to be sound.

articleTitle: Calculation of Face-SAR Due to Portable Transmitter
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to study the harmful influences of a portable transmitter on the human head, we examine numerically the face specific absorption rate (SAR) using the spherical model exposed to the near-fields of a half-wavelength dipole antenna. The spatial SAR locally averaged over one gram inside the sphere due to 915 MHz and 1250 MHz near-field exposures are calculated. The numerical results are also discussed in relation to the the exclusion criterion in the ANSI protection guide revised in 1982.

articleTitle: Near-Earth Turbulent Boundary Layer Effect on Communication Channal Transmission Coefficient Characteristics
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental studies of the channel transmission coefficient statistical characteristics in the near-earth turbulent atmosphere for the millimeter wave band are represented. The boundary layer effect can be estimated by two-frequency spatialy-temporal mutual coherence function. Theoretical investigation of this function depending on the beam and near-earth turbulent atmosphere parameters have been carried out earlier. In particular, it has been shown that the specific particuliarity of millimeter wave propagation is that the coherece function is complex. In order to verify this result experimentally, synchronous natural investigations of amplitude and angle-of-arrival fluctuations have been performed. The measurements have been carried out at 1 km and 4 km lines-of-sight in the long wave part of millimeter band. The experimental data of amplitude and angle-of-arrival fluctuation mutual correlation are found to agree with the calculation results. Spatial coherence decrease restricts the potential possibilities of antennas. The results of theoretical studies of the receiving antenna parameter dependencies on fluctuation characteristics at near-earth paths are represented.
