Numerical estimations of gain loss and spectral sensitivity in the case of linear and circular apertures have been carried out. The results of calculations show that in millimeter band the loss can reach -5dB. In the case of frequency-differente reception and also in using wideband signals the knowledge of transmission coefficient in frequency domain is needed. The study of statistical characteristics of two signals radiated at different frequencies is the key object of the estimation of atmosphere influence on channel width. Experimantal investigation of signal fluctuations frequency correlation has been carried out at 1 km and 4 km near-earht lines-of-sight. The measured data do not contradict the calculations. The experimental results show that the near-earth turbulent channel width in the long wave part of millimeter band exceeds 7.8 GHz, but it is significantly narrower than in the free atmosphere case.

articleTitle: Natural Low Frequency Electromagnetic Emissions in the Top-Side Ionosphere, the Dependence on Solar Activity
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Solar activity is a complex of various phenomena in the solar atmosphere differing by considerable variations of physical characteristics of solar atmosphere layers. These phenomena are accompanied by variations of solar energy fluxes. so, the transmission in the ultra-violet varies during the 11-year cycle upon averade by 2 times; in the X-rays - by orders of magnitude and radio and corpuscular radiation intensity during large bursts grows by many orders.

articleTitle: Barriers and State Monitoring for an EMC of Electronic Equipment of Microcomputer Based Substation Control Technique
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The mastering of EMC is an essential condition of safety land dependability for microcomputer-based control equipment in high-voltage substations. EMC is attained both by barriers formation along the possible path of interference and by barriers within the logical range of electronic circuits. Appropriate measures enable fault states to be made out to a high degree of probability and dangers to be excluded by blocking malfunktions. At that, a regular behaviour in case of interference-caused state transitions is taken into consideration in paticular as to sequential circuits. In preparing and carrying out EMC tests it is necessary that effects of barriers and gates in the interior of devices are analyzed in order to prove representative test results.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Waves Radiated from Micro-Gap Discharge in Air and SF6 Gas
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The wave shapes of micro-gap discharge currents and the radiated electromagnetic waves were measured. The results indicate that a spark-type discharge both in air and in SF<inf>6</inf> gas causes an electromagnetic radiation up to a frequency range of several hundred MHz due to its very steep front time of several nano seconds. The radiated waves, of which the level is higher than that of the background noise, can be easily detected by an antenna. But the electromagnetic waves radiated by a corona-type discharge have a relative low level, and much more difficultly to be detected using the antenna. The experimental results with a capacitive probe sensor, which was used to detect weak corona-type discharges, show that the sensor is more sensitive than the antenna.

articleTitle: Prediction of the Efficient Spectrum Utilization by Different Types of Radio-Electronic Facilities
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The procedure has been developed which when solving the problems of frequency band assignments to new radio electronic facilities (REP), makes it possible to evaluate the impact of the decisions taken on the efficiency of frequency bands sharing by future REF and REP operating in the existing network, The procedure makes it possible to take into account the effect of REF parameters defining their EMC on the efficiency of radio frequency Spectrum (RF) utilization. A prediction of possible consequences of the decisions taken permits a scientifically substantiated management of RF spectrum utilization by different REP, and the evaluation of REP parameters impact on the efficiency of spectrum utilization, serves as a basis for an introduction of technical standards for these parameters.

articleTitle: Global Electromagnetic Resonances of Earth-Ionosphere Cavity in Middle Latitudes of Asia
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the report the results of the experimental study of the Earth-ionosphere cavity global electromagnetic (Schumann) resonances in middle latitudes of Asia (Transbaikalia) have been considered. The resonance frequences f<inf>n</inf>, the Q-factor Q<inf>n</inf> and the propagation parameters ReS and d. are determined. The particularities of energy spectra obtained are discussed, the results of interpretation for different models of ionosphere are examined. It is shown that Schumann resonances may be effectively used for the Earth's crust electromagnetic sounding as well as for the characteristics definition of the cavity Earth-ionosphere.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Grid Shields
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The method of averaged boundary conditions is used to calculate tranamission coefficients of closed and open grid shields which find many applications in different fields of radioelectronics. The screen effectiveness dependence on the "grid density" parameter, cell shape, wire material is investigated. It is shown, in particular, that there is the possibility to use grid shields with unbonded wires. The shielding effect of closed screens depends very much on the frequency.

articleTitle: Influences of Electromagnetic Fields around HV Submarine Cables on Sea - and River - Fauna
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The laying of the 57 submarine cables reguires a preliminary analysis of the ecological environment along the cable from the standpoint of influence of the electromagnetic around the cables on the living organisms of the sea-end river-fauna. Shields and armours of the cables being grounded on both sides, the current flowing in the medium around the cables in the fundamental characteristic of the three phase system of cables. This current specifis all characteristics of electromagnetic field: electric and magnetic intensity, current density in the water medium.

articleTitle: Rise Time of Currents Induced on Telecommunication Cables by a Lightning Discharge
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a calculation of the current which can be induced on aerial cables by a nearby lightning stroke. Experiments performed at various triggered lightning stations such as St Privat d'Allier (France) or Floride (USA) have shown that the current of the return stroke presents a very short rise time, of few hundred nanoseconds and its derivative dI/dt reaches a mean value of about 150 kA/µs. It is thus important to determine the rise time of the current induced on cables in order to optimize the protecting devices.

articleTitle: Magnetic Coupling of Precursor Emissions at Volcano Eruption
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Authors were detected the impulsive noise bursts of seismogenic emission at 82 kHz, 1525 Hz and 36Hz by our multipoints detection network have set around the Kanto area near Tokyo region at. the time of major volcanic eruptions and related earthquakes around Izu peninsular in the last three years, such as the volcanic eruptions on November 15 and 21, 1986 at Mt. Mihara in Ohshima island, and on July 12, 1989 at Itoh Bay in Izu-peninsula region, and a minor earthquake on October 14, 1989 at Ohshima island. Since October 20, 1986, the first impulsive noise bursts at 82 kHz were recorded at Mt. Mihara in Izu-Ohshima island, and the occurrence of these anomalous burst like noise observations increased after November 3 - 14, and several strong noise bursts were observed, and the first major eruption occurred at the main summit crater of this volcano at 16 JST(Japanese Standard Time, UT+9hrs) on November 15. the second violent noise bursts were observed at 10-12 JST, and 4 hours later, 19 new craters, erupted suddenly on the side of the mountain, both inside and out side caldera. These data are the first observations of electromagnetic emissions as precursors to volcano eruptions correlated in time with the insertion of dykes in the mountain body. At July, 1989, the very locally but a serial of huge numbers of violent volcanic earthquakes were attacked suddenly to Izu Itoh city and their environmental area. Itoh city is located to east coast of Izu-peninsular and about 35 km northeast of Izu-Ohshima island, and this area is famed as a large recreation area with many hot springs. The population included environmental area of Itoh city is approximately 100 thousand. From observation results of burst like emission on 82 kHz, 1525Hz and 36 Hz at Ohshima show an interesting characteristics of the emission. This volcano was erupted in the Itoh bay from a new crater on the bottom of sea. And we show an new emission data of Just "under foot" type earthquake on October 14, 6:09:58 JST at Ohshima area. Author show the emission data at above mentioned volcanic eruption and earthquake in this paper.

articleTitle: Reduction of Interference in Observations with Synthesis Radiotelescopes
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio astronomical observations are increasingly affected by man-made interference of various kinds. Sophisticated software tools have to be developed to cope with interference effects in the data. Results of experiments with two filtering methods are discussed: [1] by rejecting data lying outside some deviation from a median for an interval running through the data cube; [2] by using a "frequency domain filtering" technique, which separates the astronomical information from the noisy background and interference effects. The tests have been done with the Westerbork Synthesis Radio Telescope and the Miyun Synthesis Radio Telescope, respectively.

articleTitle: More Studies In PLHR: Cementing a Link in the Sun-Weather Relationship?
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Previous studies [1,2] have established the existence of spatial and temporal correlations in occurrence between PLHR stimulated emissions, Auroral Absorption (AA) events, Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) flux and lightning discharges. This indirect (statistical) evidence, for a magnetosphere/atmosphere link, is supported by direct evidence [3] that the precipitation of energetic electrons (> 20 keV), due to a wave-particle interaction (WPI) at VLF, may, when meteorological conditions are appropriate, trigger lightning discharges. More recently, further examination of Ariel A data suggests that PLHR emanating from the power-lines feeding cement works in southern Canada (∧ > 55deg) near Edmonton, Winnipeg and Montreal may be having a significant effect on VLF emission and hence lightning occurrence. 3.2 kHz emission occurrence of high intensity (> 60 dB above 10<sup>−15</sup>γ<sup>2</sup>Hz<sup>−1</sup>). on field lines grounded to the east of Winnipeg (55 < ∧ < 65deg) and its geomagnetic conjugate, exceeded that, observed at any other longitude, in either hemisphere, in both northern winter and northern summer in 1971/72. More localised emission stimulation in northern winter suggests that the threshold for stimulation by a ground-based source is higher in the local winter. This appears to be consistent with observations at Siple, Antarctica [4] where the minimum radiated power for emission stimulation in the local winter was about 1 W.

articleTitle: Wave-Turbulent and Wave-Fluctuation Amplification Processes in Geophysical Hydrodynamics
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper contains a review and some new. results which reveal the substantial influence of external noise on physical processes in plasmas, gases, and liquids. We study a new kind of chaos-fluctuational chaos, which develops from weak fluctuations due to instability of moments of random fields. We show that addition of noise leads to acce location of existing instabilities and creates new ones, including fluctuational chaos. Substantial increase of transparency of opaque regions due to fluctuations of their parameters is revealed. Ve also analyze the group approach to problems of chaotic dynamics.

articleTitle: EMC and EMP in an Industrial Corona Process
publicationTitle: Tenth International Wrocław Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Over the past few years, many industrial processes have switched to electrical processes from conventional fossil fuel as a primary energy source, since electricity can be transmitted more economically than the transport of fossil fuels, as well as less pollution problems and labour- and space-saving nature. For the environmental protections, ozone generation and decomposition of pollution gas such as SO<inf>x</inf>, NO<inf>x</inf>, CO<inf>x</inf>, etc., by low temperature high pressure plasma processes become an important research subject. However, due to the early stage of development, the EMC problem is not yet well considered. In this work, we try to address the EMC problem in the various plasma processing techniques and identify future needs of research
